subjects.description: Calculus, differential equations and linear algebra foundations every engineer uses.
subjects.name: Engineering Mathematics I

topics.summary: The precise meaning of 'approaches', on which the whole of calculus is built.
topics.title: Limits & Continuity

topics.summary: Rank of a Matrix and Consistency of Linear Systems: A linear system Ax = b has solutions exactly when the coefficient matrix and the augmented matrix have the same rank; the rank then tells you whether the solution is unique or a family.
topics.title: Rank of a Matrix and Consistency of Linear Systems

topics.summary: Eigenvalues and the Characteristic Equation: An eigenvector keeps its direction under a linear map, and its eigenvalue is the factor by which the map stretches it; eigenvalues are the roots of a polynomial built from the matrix.
topics.title: Eigenvalues and the Characteristic Equation

topics.summary: Taylor Linearisation and the Size of the Error: Nearly every engineering formula in a first-year course is a truncated Taylor series, and the remainder term tells you how good the approximation is before you use it.
topics.title: Taylor Linearisation and the Size of the Error

subjects.description: Multivariable calculus, vector calculus, Laplace transforms and probability.
subjects.name: Engineering Mathematics II

topics.summary: The integrating factor that turns dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) into a derivative of a product.
topics.title: First-order linear differential equations

topics.summary: Second-Order Linear ODEs: Characteristic Roots and Damping: A constant-coefficient second-order ODE is solved by one quadratic: the roots decide whether the response decays smoothly, oscillates, or sits exactly on the boundary.
topics.title: Second-Order Linear ODEs: Characteristic Roots and Damping

topics.summary: Solving Initial-Value Problems with Laplace Transforms: The Laplace transform turns differentiation into multiplication by s, so an ODE with initial conditions becomes an algebra problem you solve and then invert.
topics.title: Solving Initial-Value Problems with Laplace Transforms

topics.summary: Bayes' Theorem and the Base-Rate Trap: A test result is not a diagnosis: the probability that a positive result means what you think it means depends on how common the condition is, and the arithmetic is unforgiving when it is rare.
topics.title: Bayes' Theorem and the Base-Rate Trap

subjects.description: Complex variables, partial differential equations, numerical methods and statistics.
subjects.name: Engineering Mathematics III

topics.summary: Fourier Series and Orthogonal Components: A periodic signal can be represented as a weighted sum of mutually orthogonal sine and cosine components.
topics.title: Fourier Series and Orthogonal Components

topics.summary: Separation of Variables for the Heat Equation: Assuming a PDE solution factors into a time part times a space part converts one hard equation into two ordinary ones joined by a single separation constant.
topics.title: Separation of Variables for the Heat Equation

topics.summary: Divergence, Curl, and the Integral Theorems: Divergence measures outward flux density and curl measures local rotation, and the integral theorems let you swap a hard surface or line integral for an easier volume or area one.
topics.title: Divergence, Curl, and the Integral Theorems

topics.summary: Newton-Raphson: Quadratic Convergence and Its Failure Modes: One iteration of Newton's method replaces the function by its tangent, and the number of correct digits doubles each step - until the derivative vanishes or the starting point is badly chosen.
topics.title: Newton-Raphson: Quadratic Convergence and Its Failure Modes

subjects.description: Waves, optics, quantum basics, semiconductors and materials for engineers.
subjects.name: Engineering Physics

topics.summary: The physics behind every diode, transistor and chip - and why doping changes everything.
topics.title: Semiconductors & PN Junctions

topics.summary: Double-Slit Interference and Fringe Spacing: Overlapping waves from two narrow slits add or cancel by path difference, producing bright fringes whose spacing measures the wavelength.
topics.title: Double-Slit Interference and Fringe Spacing

topics.summary: Photoelectric Effect and Work Function: Electrons are ejected only when each photon individually carries more energy than the metal's work function; brighter light adds electrons but never energy per electron.
topics.title: Photoelectric Effect and Work Function

topics.summary: Thin-Film Interference and Anti-Reflection Coatings: A quarter-wave film makes two reflected waves cancel, which is how a lens is made almost non-reflective at one wavelength - and the arithmetic is a single division.
topics.title: Thin-Film Interference and Anti-Reflection Coatings

subjects.description: Electrochemistry, polymers, fuels, corrosion and water treatment.
subjects.name: Engineering Chemistry

topics.summary: PV = nRT, the units that make R true, and when a real gas stops obeying it.
topics.title: The ideal gas law

topics.summary: Cell Potential and the Nernst Equation: A galvanic cell's voltage is its standard potential corrected for the actual concentrations the reaction quotient reports.
topics.title: Cell Potential and the Nernst Equation

topics.summary: Corrosion Cells and Cathodic Protection: Corrosion is a short-circuited electrochemical cell: the more active metal becomes the anode and dissolves, and protection works by forcing that role onto a cheaper metal.
topics.title: Corrosion Cells and Cathodic Protection

topics.summary: Buffers and the Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation: A buffer resists pH change because it contains both members of an acid-base pair, and the ratio of their concentrations sets where it holds.
topics.title: Buffers and the Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation

subjects.description: Projections, orthographic views, sections and isometric drawing standards.
subjects.name: Engineering Graphics

topics.summary: Orthographic Projection and Scale: Orthographic views use parallel projectors to show true dimensions on faces parallel to the projection plane.
topics.title: Orthographic Projection and Scale

topics.summary: Isometric Projection and the Isometric Scale: An isometric view tilts the object so three faces show at once, and true isometric projection shrinks every edge by a fixed factor.
topics.title: Isometric Projection and the Isometric Scale

topics.summary: Assembly Drawings and the Bill of Materials: An assembly drawing is a contract between design and production: every ballooned part must trace to exactly one BOM row, and the BOM is what procurement actually buys.
topics.title: Assembly Drawings and the Bill of Materials

topics.summary: True Length and Inclination from Orthographic Projections: A line appears shortened in every orthographic view unless it is parallel to the plane of projection, and its true length is recovered from one view plus the distance difference in the other.
topics.title: True Length and Inclination from Orthographic Projections

subjects.description: Drafting standards plus modern CAD workflow and dimensioning.
subjects.name: Engineering Drawing & CAD

topics.summary: Limits, Fits, and Tolerance: A tolerance is the allowed interval around a nominal dimension that lets parts function and assemble reliably.
topics.title: Limits, Fits, and Tolerance

topics.summary: Datums and Feature Control Frames in GD&T: Geometric tolerancing controls shape and location relative to named datums, and material-condition modifiers let a feature earn extra tolerance when it is made smaller or larger than its worst case.
topics.title: Datums and Feature Control Frames in GD&T

topics.summary: Threaded Fasteners: Designation, Pitch and Tap Drills: A thread callout like M10 x 1.5 encodes everything a shop needs - major diameter and pitch - and the tap drill follows from how much material the threads must leave.
topics.title: Threaded Fasteners: Designation, Pitch and Tap Drills

topics.summary: Position Tolerance at Maximum Material Condition: A hole made at its maximum size can be offset further and still assemble, and that bonus tolerance is what makes the maximum-material modifier useful on production drawings.
topics.title: Position Tolerance at Maximum Material Condition

subjects.description: DC/AC circuits, network theorems, transformers and machines.
subjects.name: Basic Electrical Engineering

topics.summary: Why voltage and current can be out of step in AC systems, and what that costs you.
topics.title: AC Circuits & Power Factor

topics.summary: Three-Phase Star and Delta Relationships: In a balanced three-phase system the connection topology alone fixes the sqrt(3) relationship between line and phase quantities.
topics.title: Three-Phase Star and Delta Relationships

topics.summary: Series RLC Resonance, Bandwidth and Q: At one frequency the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, the series circuit looks purely resistive, and the sharpness of that peak is set by Q.
topics.title: Series RLC Resonance, Bandwidth and Q

topics.summary: The Two-Wattmeter Method for Three-Phase Power: Two wattmeters measure total active power in a balanced three-phase load and, from the difference of their readings, reactive power and power factor as well.
topics.title: The Two-Wattmeter Method for Three-Phase Power

subjects.description: Diodes, BJTs, op-amps, digital logic and instrumentation basics.
subjects.name: Basic Electronics

topics.summary: Diode Bias and Series Current: A forward-biased diode conducts while a resistor limits current; the source voltage is shared by both.
topics.title: Diode Bias and Series Current

topics.summary: BJT Biasing and the DC Load Line: A transistor amplifier only works where the DC bias parks it, and the load line shows every combination of current and voltage the external circuit permits.
topics.title: BJT Biasing and the DC Load Line

topics.summary: Rectification: Average Output and Ripple: A bridge rectifier folds the negative half-cycles upright, doubling the average output and halving the ripple period compared with a single diode.
topics.title: Rectification: Average Output and Ripple

topics.summary: Zener Shunt Regulator: Series Resistor and Dissipation Limits: A shunt regulator holds its output at the breakdown voltage by burning the difference between source and load current, so the design is a two-case calculation: the resistor for minimum input, the zener for maximum input.
topics.title: Zener Shunt Regulator: Series Resistor and Dissipation Limits

subjects.description: Your first programming language: logic, control flow, functions and arrays.
subjects.name: Programming Fundamentals

topics.summary: How a program names and manipulates data - and the type rules that catch mistakes before they run.
topics.title: Variables, Data Types & Operators

topics.summary: Directing which statements run and how many times - the basis of every algorithm you will ever write.
topics.title: Control Flow: Conditionals & Loops

topics.summary: Functions, Scope, and the Call Stack: Every call pushes an activation record holding arguments, locals and the return address; scope rules decide which names a line of code can see, and the stack decides what exists right now.
topics.title: Functions, Scope, and the Call Stack

topics.summary: Big-O Reasoning for Loops and Nested Loops: Counting how often the inner statement executes as input grows is all that is needed to classify most everyday code - nesting multiplies, sequence adds.
topics.title: Big-O Reasoning for Loops and Nested Loops

topics.summary: String Building, Immutability and the Cost of Repeated Concatenation: Appending to an immutable string inside a loop copies the whole string each time, turning a linear job quadratic - the classic first lesson in choosing the right primitive.
topics.title: String Building, Immutability and the Cost of Repeated Concatenation

subjects.description: Statics, force systems, friction, trusses and rigid body equilibrium.
subjects.name: Engineering Mechanics

topics.summary: The single most important skill in mechanics: isolating a body and drawing every force on it.
topics.title: Equilibrium of Forces & Free Body Diagrams

topics.summary: Friction: Static Limit, Kinetic Slide and the Friction Angle: Static friction matches the applied push up to a ceiling of mu_s N; past that ceiling the body slides with a smaller, roughly constant kinetic friction.
topics.title: Friction: Static Limit, Kinetic Slide and the Friction Angle

topics.summary: Method of Joints for Plane Trusses: Every truss member carries only axial force, so each pin joint is a concurrent-force problem solvable with two equilibrium equations - if you visit joints in an order that never presents more than two unknowns.
topics.title: Method of Joints for Plane Trusses

topics.summary: Composite Sections: Centroid and Second Moment of Area: A section's bending stiffness is not its area: the same material placed further from the neutral axis resists bending far better, and the parallel-axis theorem quantifies exactly how much.
topics.title: Composite Sections: Centroid and Second Moment of Area

subjects.description: Technical writing, presentations and interview communication.
subjects.name: Communication Skills

topics.summary: Writing a Decision-Ready Engineering Brief: A useful technical brief states the decision, supports it with traceable evidence, and makes the next action explicit.
topics.title: Writing a Decision-Ready Engineering Brief

topics.summary: Structuring Technical Presentations with the Pyramid Principle: Decision audiences retain an answer-first structure: the recommendation on slide one, grouped supporting arguments beneath it, evidence at the bottom.
topics.title: Structuring Technical Presentations with the Pyramid Principle

topics.summary: Reading Charts Honestly: Axes, Scales and Visual Distortion: A chart's visual message is the ratio its ink shows; when the axis is truncated or the scale is uneven, that ratio silently exaggerates the data ratio.
topics.title: Reading Charts Honestly: Axes, Scales and Visual Distortion

topics.summary: Sentence Length, Readability Formulas and Editing for Skimming: Technical writing is read by people who are short of time, so structure and sentence length decide whether the content is received; readability formulas turn that into arithmetic, imperfectly but usefully.
topics.title: Sentence Length, Readability Formulas and Editing for Skimming

subjects.description: Ecosystems, pollution, sustainability and environmental law.
subjects.name: Environmental Studies

topics.summary: The IPAT Model for Environmental Impact: The IPAT identity separates environmental impact into population, consumption per person, and impact per unit of consumption.
topics.title: The IPAT Model for Environmental Impact

topics.summary: Scope 1, 2 and 3 Greenhouse-Gas Accounting: A carbon footprint is only auditable once emissions are split by ownership: what you burn, what your purchased energy burned, and what your value chain burned.
topics.title: Scope 1, 2 and 3 Greenhouse-Gas Accounting

topics.summary: BOD and Dissolved Oxygen as Water-Quality Indicators: Biochemical oxygen demand measures how much oxygen microbes will consume stabilising the organic load - the same oxygen a river must spare for fish.
topics.title: BOD and Dissolved Oxygen as Water-Quality Indicators

topics.summary: Grid Emission Factors: Average, Marginal and What a Saving Really Avoids: Every kilowatt hour saved avoids a different amount of carbon depending on which generator would have supplied it, and the difference between average and marginal factors is where most carbon claims go wrong.
topics.title: Grid Emission Factors: Average, Marginal and What a Saving Really Avoids

subjects.description: Fitting, smithy, welding, carpentry and safety on the shop floor.
subjects.name: Workshop Practice

topics.summary: Cutting Speed in Turning Operations: Cutting speed is the tangential speed of the work surface at the cutting edge and sets the spindle-speed relationship.
topics.title: Cutting Speed in Turning Operations

topics.summary: Drilling: Cutting Speed, Spindle RPM and Feed: The material sets the cutting speed at the edge; the drill diameter converts that speed into the spindle RPM the machine must actually turn.
topics.title: Drilling: Cutting Speed, Spindle RPM and Feed

topics.summary: Sheet-Metal Bend Allowance and Flat Development: Bent sheet parts are cut flat, so the flat pattern must add back the arc length the neutral axis travels through each bend - the bend allowance.
topics.title: Sheet-Metal Bend Allowance and Flat Development

topics.summary: Surface Roughness from Feed and Tool Nose Radius: The theoretical roughness left by a turning tool is set by the feed and the nose radius, and the squared feed term explains why halving the feed improves the finish fourfold.
topics.title: Surface Roughness from Feed and Tool Nose Radius

subjects.description: The single highest-leverage subject in computing - and the core of every interview.
subjects.name: Data Structures & Algorithms

topics.summary: Contiguous memory holding fixed-size elements, giving O(1) indexed access - the foundation every other structure is measured against.
topics.title: Arrays

topics.summary: Nodes chained by pointers, giving O(1) insertion at a known position at the cost of O(n) access.
topics.title: Linked Lists

topics.summary: Two restricted access patterns - LIFO and FIFO - that turn out to solve an enormous number of problems.
topics.title: Stacks & Queues

topics.summary: Hierarchical nodes with at most two children, plus the four traversal orders that unlock almost every tree problem.
topics.title: Binary Trees & Traversals

topics.summary: A binary tree with an ordering invariant that makes search, insertion and deletion logarithmic - when it stays balanced.
topics.title: Binary Search Trees

topics.summary: Key-to-value mapping with expected O(1) operations, built on a hash function plus collision resolution.
topics.title: Hash Tables

topics.summary: A complete binary tree that keeps the extreme element on top, giving O(log n) updates and O(1) peek.
topics.title: Heaps & Priority Queues

topics.summary: Vertices and edges modelling arbitrary relationships, with BFS and DFS as the two universal exploration strategies.
topics.title: Graphs & Traversals

topics.summary: Solving a problem once per subproblem and reusing the answer, turning exponential recursion into polynomial iteration.
topics.title: Dynamic Programming

topics.summary: The classic sorting algorithms and the comparison-based lower bound that explains why O(n log n) is the best you can do.
topics.title: Sorting & Complexity

topics.summary: Solving a problem by solving smaller copies of itself, and exploring a decision tree with pruning.
topics.title: Recursion & Backtracking

topics.summary: Shortest Paths: Dijkstra and Edge Relaxation: Dijkstra's algorithm locks in the cheapest known distance to one vertex at a time, and every lock-in is justified by relaxing edges out of the just-settled vertex.
topics.title: Shortest Paths: Dijkstra and Edge Relaxation

topics.summary: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Arrays and the Accounting Method: A single array append can cost O(n) during a resize, but charged across the whole sequence the average cost per operation stays constant - amortized analysis proves the difference between worst-case-per-op and worst-case-per-sequence.
topics.title: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Arrays and the Accounting Method

topics.summary: Union-Find with Path Compression: A disjoint-set forest answers 'are these two elements connected?' in effectively constant time by attaching smaller trees under larger ones and flattening every path that a find walks.
topics.title: Union-Find with Path Compression

subjects.description: Classes, inheritance, polymorphism and how to model real systems.
subjects.name: Object Oriented Programming

topics.summary: The three mechanisms that let object-oriented code stay understandable as it grows.
topics.title: Encapsulation, Inheritance & Polymorphism

topics.summary: Reusable solutions to recurring design problems - and the discipline to know when not to use one.
topics.title: Design Patterns

topics.summary: SOLID Principles Applied to a Small Design: SOLID is a checklist for decisions you already face: who owns a behaviour, what may change independently, and which direction dependencies are allowed to point.
topics.title: SOLID Principles Applied to a Small Design

topics.summary: Composition over Inheritance and Object Lifetimes: Inheritance shares an implementation and a type forever; composition shares behaviour by holding a reference you can swap, which keeps change local and lifetimes explicit.
topics.title: Composition over Inheritance and Object Lifetimes

topics.summary: Coupling Metrics and the Dependency-Pointing Rule: Package level coupling can be measured and then governed: a package's instability is the share of its dependencies that point outward, and stable packages are the ones that must be abstract.
topics.title: Coupling Metrics and the Dependency-Pointing Rule

subjects.description: Relational modelling, SQL, normalisation, indexing and transactions.
subjects.name: Database Management Systems

topics.summary: Removing redundant data so updates cannot contradict themselves - and knowing when to deliberately stop.
topics.title: Normalization

topics.summary: Why a query takes 3 seconds instead of 3 milliseconds, and the index that fixes it.
topics.title: Indexes & Query Performance

topics.summary: The guarantees that make a database trustworthy when things crash halfway through.
topics.title: Transactions & ACID

topics.summary: Combining rows across tables and summarising them - the day-to-day language of every data role.
topics.title: SQL Joins & Aggregation

topics.summary: B-Tree Indexes: Fan-Out and Logarithmic Search: An index is a search structure shaped for disks: each node holds many keys so the tree stays shallow, and height - not key count - decides how many block reads a lookup costs.
topics.title: B-Tree Indexes: Fan-Out and Logarithmic Search

topics.summary: Relational Algebra: Selection, Projection and Join: Every SQL query is a relational-algebra expression in disguise, and reading queries as algebra shows what the optimizer is allowed to reorder.
topics.title: Relational Algebra: Selection, Projection and Join

topics.summary: Query Cost: Selectivity and the Index Break-Even Point: A planner chooses an index over a table scan when the rows it would fetch are a small enough fraction of the table; that break-even point is a computation you can reproduce.
topics.title: Query Cost: Selectivity and the Index Break-Even Point

subjects.description: Processes, scheduling, memory, file systems and concurrency.
subjects.name: Operating Systems

topics.summary: The unit of execution and the unit of scheduling - and why the distinction matters for isolation, cost and concurrency.
topics.title: Processes & Threads

topics.summary: Deciding which ready process runs next, and the metrics that tell you whether the decision was good.
topics.title: CPU Scheduling

topics.summary: Four conditions that must all hold for processes to freeze forever, and the strategies for breaking each one.
topics.title: Deadlocks

topics.summary: How the OS gives every process a private, contiguous-looking address space using pages and a page table.
topics.title: Memory Management & Paging

topics.summary: Coordinating concurrent access to shared state so results stay correct - and the classic problems that show why it is hard.
topics.title: Synchronisation & Semaphores

topics.summary: How bytes on a disk become named, permissioned, journaled files - and what actually happens when you save.
topics.title: File Systems

topics.summary: Page Replacement: FIFO, LRU and Belady's Anomaly: When every frame is full, the victim-page rule decides the fault count - and FIFO's rule is so naive that adding memory can make it worse.
topics.title: Page Replacement: FIFO, LRU and Belady's Anomaly

topics.summary: Banker's Algorithm and Safe Sequences: Deadlock avoidance grants a request only if the system can still prove a completion order exists for every process with the resources left over.
topics.title: Banker's Algorithm and Safe Sequences

topics.summary: Effective Access Time and the Fault-Rate Budget: The cost of virtual memory is decided by one product: page-fault rate times fault service time, which sets the maximum fault rate a system can tolerate for a given slowdown.
topics.title: Effective Access Time and the Fault-Rate Budget

subjects.description: The layered model from physical signals to TCP and HTTP.
subjects.name: Computer Networks

topics.summary: The layered abstraction that lets a web request travel through cables, routers and satellites without any layer knowing the others' details.
topics.title: OSI & TCP/IP Models

topics.summary: How two hosts agree on reliable, ordered delivery over an unreliable network.
topics.title: TCP & Flow Control

topics.summary: Dividing a network into smaller ones so addresses scale and broadcast traffic stays local.
topics.title: IP Addressing & Subnetting

topics.summary: Congestion Control: Slow Start and AIMD: TCP discovers the network's capacity by probing multiplicatively and backing off multiplicatively, converging to fairness without any router telling it the answer.
topics.title: Congestion Control: Slow Start and AIMD

topics.summary: Distance-Vector Routing and Count-to-Infinity: Routers believing only their neighbours' rumours can trap a stale path in a two-node loop that climbs one hop-cost at a time toward infinity.
topics.title: Distance-Vector Routing and Count-to-Infinity

topics.summary: Bandwidth-Delay Product and Window Sizing: A transport window that is smaller than the path's bandwidth-delay product wastes the link: throughput becomes window divided by round-trip time, whatever the capacity says.
topics.title: Bandwidth-Delay Product and Window Sizing

subjects.description: How a processor actually executes your code, and why caches matter.
subjects.name: Computer Organization & Architecture

topics.summary: Why the memory hierarchy exists and how writing cache-friendly code can be worth more than a better algorithm.
topics.title: Cache Memory & Locality

topics.summary: Pipelining: Hazards, Stalls and Real Speedup: A k-stage pipeline promises k-fold throughput, but data, control and structural hazards tax the promise; the honest speedup divides by the stall cycles actually paid.
topics.title: Pipelining: Hazards, Stalls and Real Speedup

topics.summary: The CPU Performance Equation and Amdahl's Law: Program time is instructions times cycles-per-instruction divided by clock rate, and Amdahl's law caps what speeding up any one part can do for the whole.
topics.title: The CPU Performance Equation and Amdahl's Law

topics.summary: Miss Rates and Average Memory Access Time Across Cache Levels: Memory performance is a sum of expected penalties: each level's miss rate multiplies the cost of the level beneath it, so a small improvement where misses are frequent beats a large one where they are rare.
topics.title: Miss Rates and Average Memory Access Time Across Cache Levels

subjects.description: Automata, grammars, decidability and the limits of computation.
subjects.name: Theory of Computation

topics.summary: A finite set of states, one start, a transition for every symbol, and a language of accepted strings.
topics.title: Deterministic finite automata

topics.summary: The Pumping Lemma and Non-Regular Languages: Every sufficiently long string accepted by a finite automaton contains a loop, and re-traversing that loop must stay inside the language - one contradiction away from proving non-regularity.
topics.title: The Pumping Lemma and Non-Regular Languages

topics.summary: Context-Free Grammars, Parse Trees and Ambiguity: A grammar generates a language by rewriting variables, and a string's parse tree is the derivation made visible - ambiguous grammars hand the same string two different trees.
topics.title: Context-Free Grammars, Parse Trees and Ambiguity

topics.summary: Myhill-Nerode Classes and Minimal Automata: The minimal DFA for a language has exactly one state per Myhill-Nerode equivalence class, so the number of classes is both an achievable design and a proof that no smaller one exists.
topics.title: Myhill-Nerode Classes and Minimal Automata

subjects.description: Lexing, parsing, semantic analysis and code generation.
subjects.name: Compiler Design

topics.summary: The front of a compiler turns characters into tokens before any grammar runs.
topics.title: Lexical analysis

topics.summary: LL(1) Parsing: FIRST and FOLLOW Sets: A predictive parser chooses each production from one lookahead token, which works exactly when the alternatives' prediction sets do not overlap.
topics.title: LL(1) Parsing: FIRST and FOLLOW Sets

topics.summary: Three-Address Code and Intermediate Representations: Between source and machine code a compiler rewrites programs into small fixed-shape instructions, so optimization can run once on the IR instead of once per source language and once per target.
topics.title: Three-Address Code and Intermediate Representations

topics.summary: Strength Reduction and the Address-Calculation Cost Model: Inside a loop, replacing a multiplication by a running addition removes work from every iteration; the saving is the per-iteration difference times the trip count, which is small on modern silicon but decisive on embedded cores.
topics.title: Strength Reduction and the Address-Calculation Cost Model

subjects.description: Process models, requirements, design, testing and quality.
subjects.name: Software Engineering

topics.summary: How teams plan, build and verify software - and the testing pyramid that keeps quality affordable.
topics.title: Software Process Models & Testing

topics.summary: Cyclomatic Complexity and Basis Path Testing: The number of independent paths through a routine is a small integer you can compute from its flow graph - and it is the minimum count of tests that can claim to have exercised its logic.
topics.title: Cyclomatic Complexity and Basis Path Testing

topics.summary: Effort Estimation: Function Points and COCOMO: Estimation models trade a size measurement for an effort number, and both classic models agree on one thing: effort grows superlinearly with size.
topics.title: Effort Estimation: Function Points and COCOMO

topics.summary: Defect Removal Efficiency and Release Readiness: Release readiness is a ratio, not a feeling: the share of defects found before release, and the sample size needed to reach a target.
topics.title: Defect Removal Efficiency and Release Readiness

subjects.description: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning with real maths.
subjects.name: Machine Learning

topics.summary: Gradient Descent and Loss Minimization: Gradient descent updates model parameters opposite the loss gradient so a small step locally reduces error.
topics.title: Gradient Descent and Loss Minimization

topics.summary: Bias-Variance Decomposition and Model Selection: Prediction error splits into squared bias, variance and irreducible noise, and the split explains why bigger models can test worse: they trade bias for variance.
topics.title: Bias-Variance Decomposition and Model Selection

topics.summary: Precision, Recall and the F1 Score: Accuracy hides class imbalance; precision and recall expose the two distinct mistakes a classifier can make, and F1 forces a single number to face both.
topics.title: Precision, Recall and the F1 Score

topics.summary: Ridge Regularisation and Numerical Conditioning: Adding a squared penalty turns an ill-posed least-squares problem into a well-conditioned one, at the cost of a deliberate, quantifiable shrinkage of the coefficients.
topics.title: Ridge Regularisation and Numerical Conditioning

subjects.description: Neural networks, CNNs, transformers and training at scale.
subjects.name: Deep Learning

topics.summary: Backpropagation and the Chain Rule: Backpropagation reuses local derivatives through a computation graph to obtain the loss gradient for each parameter.
topics.title: Backpropagation and the Chain Rule

topics.summary: Vanishing Gradients and Activation Choice: Backpropagation multiplies per-layer derivatives on the way down; activations whose derivatives are small shrink early-layer learning exponentially with depth.
topics.title: Vanishing Gradients and Activation Choice

topics.summary: Regularization: Dropout and Weight Decay: Both techniques buy generalization by constraining what the network is allowed to do - dropout by randomly deleting units during training, weight decay by penalizing large weights.
topics.title: Regularization: Dropout and Weight Decay

topics.summary: Initialisation Variance and Signal Preservation: A network trains because variance is preserved across layers; the standard initialisers are exactly the weight variance that keeps the forward pass from collapsing or exploding.
topics.title: Initialisation Variance and Signal Preservation

subjects.description: Statistics, data wrangling and visualisation for engineers.
subjects.name: Data Science Foundations

topics.summary: Standardization and the Z-Score: A z-score expresses how many standard deviations an observation lies from a reference mean.
topics.title: Standardization and the Z-Score

topics.summary: Sampling Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem: A statistic computed from random samples is itself a random variable with its own distribution, and the CLT says averages look normal with a standard error that shrinks as sqrt(n).
topics.title: Sampling Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem

topics.summary: Pearson Correlation: Computation and Its Limits: The correlation coefficient standardizes covariance to [-1, 1] so linear association becomes comparable across datasets - and 'linear' is the word that gets forgotten.
topics.title: Pearson Correlation: Computation and Its Limits

topics.summary: Margin of Error, Sample Size and Multiple Comparisons: A confidence interval's width is decided before the study by three numbers - variability, confidence level and sample size - and testing many hypotheses at once inflates false positives unless the threshold is adjusted.
topics.title: Margin of Error, Sample Size and Multiple Comparisons

subjects.description: Symmetric and public key crypto, hashes, TLS and attack models.
subjects.name: Cryptography & Network Security

topics.summary: Threat Modeling and Security Objectives: A threat model names assets, trust boundaries, adversaries, and abuse cases before controls are selected.
topics.title: Threat Modeling and Security Objectives

topics.summary: Password Storage: Salts and Slow Password Hashing: A server stores a salted, deliberately expensive password verifier rather than plaintext or a fast general-purpose hash.
topics.title: Password Storage: Salts and Slow Password Hashing

topics.summary: Authenticated Encryption and Nonce Discipline: Authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) protects ciphertext confidentiality and detects tampering in one construction.
topics.title: Authenticated Encryption and Nonce Discipline

topics.summary: TLS Certificates and Server Identity Validation: TLS protects a channel only when the client validates the certificate chain and the requested hostname before trusting the peer.
topics.title: TLS Certificates and Server Identity Validation

topics.summary: Parameterized Queries and Injection Prevention: Parameterized database calls keep SQL structure separate from untrusted values so input is interpreted as data, not executable syntax.
topics.title: Parameterized Queries and Injection Prevention

topics.summary: Safe Input Boundaries: SQL, NoSQL, and Template Injection: Untrusted input stays data when servers validate its shape, bind query values, and never compile user-controlled text as a template.
topics.title: Safe Input Boundaries: SQL, NoSQL, and Template Injection

topics.summary: Availability Controls: ReDoS, Long Passwords, and Rate Limits: Bound every attacker-controlled unit of work so pathological regular expressions, oversized passwords, and request floods cannot consume unlimited resources.
topics.title: Availability Controls: ReDoS, Long Passwords, and Rate Limits

topics.summary: Authentication, Authorization, and Replay-Safe Sessions: Authentication establishes who is acting; authorization checks what that identity may do on every protected request.
topics.title: Authentication, Authorization, and Replay-Safe Sessions

topics.summary: Secrets Management, Error Hygiene, and Audit Privacy: Credentials stay outside source control and untrusted request values stay out of error messages, analytics, and audit metadata.
topics.title: Secrets Management, Error Hygiene, and Audit Privacy

topics.summary: Safe File Uploads and Clipboard Trust Boundaries: Treat uploaded files and pasted clipboard content as hostile input until the server validates and the user explicitly chooses what to do with it.
topics.title: Safe File Uploads and Clipboard Trust Boundaries

topics.summary: Secure Delivery, Dependency Risk, and Incident Readiness: Security is a lifecycle property: review dependencies, verify changes, monitor safe signals, and practise recovery before an incident.
topics.title: Secure Delivery, Dependency Risk, and Incident Readiness

topics.summary: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange and Forward Secrecy: Two parties can agree on a secret over a public channel because exponentiation is easy while discrete logarithms are not - and ephemeral keys turn that agreement into forward secrecy.
topics.title: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange and Forward Secrecy

topics.summary: Hash Functions, Integrity and the Length-Extension Pitfall: A cryptographic hash compresses any message to a fixed fingerprint that is collision-resistant and one-way - but Merkle-Damgard designs leak a forgery channel if you improvise a MAC from them.
topics.title: Hash Functions, Integrity and the Length-Extension Pitfall

topics.summary: Collision Resistance and the Birthday Bound: The security level of a hash is not its output size: collisions are found in about the square root of the output space, so a 256-bit digest is a 128-bit commitment.
topics.title: Collision Resistance and the Birthday Bound

subjects.description: Virtualisation, elasticity, distributed storage and serverless.
subjects.name: Cloud Computing

topics.summary: Service Availability and Error Budgets: Availability is the fraction of observed service time that meets the agreed service condition.
topics.title: Service Availability and Error Budgets

topics.summary: Autoscaling Signals: Target Utilization and Replica Math: An autoscaler is a control loop: measure aggregate load, divide by what one replica should carry, and converge the replica count to the ceiling of that ratio.
topics.title: Autoscaling Signals: Target Utilization and Replica Math

topics.summary: Cloud Cost Trade-Offs: Reserved versus On-Demand Break-Even: A reserved instance is a bet on future utilization; the break-even hours formula prices that bet exactly.
topics.title: Cloud Cost Trade-Offs: Reserved versus On-Demand Break-Even

topics.summary: Queueing Headroom and Replica Sizing: Capacity is not max throughput divided by per-replica throughput: because waiting time grows without bound as utilisation approaches one, replicas are sized to a utilisation ceiling, not to the peak.
topics.title: Queueing Headroom and Replica Sizing

subjects.description: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, HTTP and modern full-stack patterns.
subjects.name: Web Technologies

topics.summary: HTTP Requests, Responses, and Safe State Changes: HTTP separates a request's method, target, headers, and optional body from a response's status, headers, and representation.
topics.title: HTTP Requests, Responses, and Safe State Changes

topics.summary: Cache Headers, ETags and Conditional Requests: HTTP caching is a freshness contract: max-age says how long a copy stays usable silently, and validators let a stale copy be reconfirmed cheaply instead of refetched.
topics.title: Cache Headers, ETags and Conditional Requests

topics.summary: Same-Origin Policy and CORS Preflight: The same-origin policy is the browser's default wall between sites, and CORS is the origin's explicit, header-signed permission slip for named outsiders.
topics.title: Same-Origin Policy and CORS Preflight

topics.summary: Freshness Lifetimes and Origin Load: Caching reduces origin load as a function of freshness lifetime, and the same arithmetic predicts the stampede that a deployment can cause when every cached object expires at once.
topics.title: Freshness Lifetimes and Origin Load

subjects.description: Logic, sets, relations, graph theory and combinatorics.
subjects.name: Discrete Mathematics

topics.summary: Membership, ordered pairs, and the rule that a function gives each input one output.
topics.title: Sets, relations and functions

topics.summary: Counting: Permutations, Combinations and Pigeonhole: Order matters in permutations and not in combinations, and the pigeonhole principle turns any surplus of items over boxes into a guaranteed collision.
topics.title: Counting: Permutations, Combinations and Pigeonhole

topics.summary: Degrees, Paths and Euler Circuits in Graphs: Every edge contributes two degrees, so degree sums count edges twice - and that simple parity fact decides when a graph can be drawn in one continuous stroke.
topics.title: Degrees, Paths and Euler Circuits in Graphs

topics.summary: Recurrences, Characteristic Roots and Closed Forms: A linear recurrence describes cost, count or state growth; its characteristic roots turn the recursion into a closed form whose dominant root is the growth rate.
topics.title: Recurrences, Characteristic Roots and Closed Forms

subjects.description: Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits.
subjects.name: Digital Logic Design

topics.summary: How unsigned binary counts, and how a fixed width represents a negative integer.
topics.title: Binary numbers and two's complement

topics.summary: Multiplexers and Decoders as Combinational Building Blocks: A 2^n-to-1 multiplexer routes one of 2^n data inputs to the output by an n-bit select, which makes it a lookup table in hardware - and any Boolean function can be wired into its data inputs.
topics.title: Multiplexers and Decoders as Combinational Building Blocks

topics.summary: Flip-Flop Timing: Setup, Hold and Maximum Clock Rate: A flip-flop samples correctly only if data is stable around the clock edge, and those stability windows set the shortest legal clock period of the whole synchronous system.
topics.title: Flip-Flop Timing: Setup, Hold and Maximum Clock Rate

topics.summary: Adder Carry Chains: Ripple Depth versus Lookahead: An adder's speed is set by how long its carry takes to cross the word: a ripple chain costs n full-adder delays, and grouping the carry logic turns that into a logarithmic depth.
topics.title: Adder Carry Chains: Ripple Depth versus Lookahead

subjects.description: Energy, entropy and the laws that govern every engine and power plant.
subjects.name: Engineering Thermodynamics

topics.summary: Why some processes never happen in reverse, and the quantity that measures the direction of time.
topics.title: Entropy & the Second Law

topics.summary: Energy accounting for a system: what goes in, what comes out, and what is stored.
topics.title: First Law & Energy Balance

topics.summary: Carnot Efficiency and the Reversible Limit: No engine between two temperatures can beat the Carnot fraction, so the second law hands every heat engine a ceiling computed from temperatures alone.
topics.title: Carnot Efficiency and the Reversible Limit

topics.summary: Otto Cycle: Compression Ratio and Efficiency: The spark-ignition engine's ideal efficiency is fixed by one geometric number - the compression ratio - raised to a power set by the gas.
topics.title: Otto Cycle: Compression Ratio and Efficiency

topics.summary: Nozzle Flow: Enthalpy Drop to Exit Velocity: A nozzle converts enthalpy into kinetic energy, so the exit velocity follows from the enthalpy drop alone - and the speed of sound tells you whether the flow is choked.
topics.title: Nozzle Flow: Enthalpy Drop to Exit Velocity

subjects.description: Statics, kinematics and dynamics of fluids - Bernoulli to boundary layers.
subjects.name: Fluid Mechanics

topics.summary: Energy conservation for a flowing fluid: pressure, velocity and elevation trade against each other along a streamline.
topics.title: Bernoulli's Equation

topics.summary: Pressure in a fluid at rest, and how a simple column of liquid measures it.
topics.title: Fluid Statics & Manometry

topics.summary: Darcy-Weisbach Friction Loss in Pipe Flow: Head loss along a pipe is a dimensionless friction factor times a velocity head, scaled by how much pipe the flow traverses - the workhorse of every piping calculation.
topics.title: Darcy-Weisbach Friction Loss in Pipe Flow

topics.summary: Drag Force and Terminal Velocity: A body moving through fluid pays a force proportional to velocity squared, and free fall ends when that force balances weight - the terminal velocity.
topics.title: Drag Force and Terminal Velocity

topics.summary: Minor Losses and Equivalent Length: Fittings, valves and bends cost head that is usually written as a multiple of the velocity head, and converting it into an equivalent length of straight pipe shows whether it can be ignored.
topics.title: Minor Losses and Equivalent Length

subjects.description: Stress, strain, bending, torsion and how things fail.
subjects.name: Strength of Materials

topics.summary: How materials respond to load, and the linear region every design lives inside.
topics.title: Stress, Strain & Hooke's Law

topics.summary: Bending Stress and Section Modulus: A beam's fibres stretch and compress linearly through its depth, so bending stress peaks at the extreme fibre and the section modulus packages the geometry that resists it.
topics.title: Bending Stress and Section Modulus

topics.summary: Torsion of Circular Shafts: A circular shaft under torque develops shear stress rising linearly to its surface, and the polar second moment packages the geometry that carries the twist.
topics.title: Torsion of Circular Shafts

topics.summary: Combined Loading: Principal Stresses and the von Mises Criterion: A component under simultaneous bending, torsion and axial load fails according to a criterion applied to a single equivalent stress, and both the principal stresses and that equivalent are computed from the same three numbers.
topics.title: Combined Loading: Principal Stresses and the von Mises Criterion

subjects.description: Casting, forming, machining, joining and additive manufacturing.
subjects.name: Manufacturing Processes

topics.summary: Machining Parameters: Speed, Feed, and Material Removal: A machining process is controlled by tool/work speed, feed per revolution, depth of cut, and the material-tool pair.
topics.title: Machining Parameters: Speed, Feed, and Material Removal

topics.summary: Casting: Chvorinov's Rule and Riser Design: Solidification time scales with the square of a casting's volume-to-surface ratio - the rule that decides riser size, placement and whether a casting shrinks sound or porous.
topics.title: Casting: Chvorinov's Rule and Riser Design

topics.summary: Welding Heat Input and Joint Integrity: Heat input per unit length decides the weld's cooling rate, and cooling rate decides the microstructure, hardness and crack risk of the joint - it is the number procedure specs control.
topics.title: Welding Heat Input and Joint Integrity

topics.summary: Blanking Force and Die Clearance: Punching a shape out of sheet needs a press whose force covers the whole cut perimeter at once, and a clearance between punch and die set as a fraction of sheet thickness.
topics.title: Blanking Force and Die Clearance

subjects.description: Designing shafts, gears, springs, bearings and welded joints for real loads.
subjects.name: Machine Design

topics.summary: Factor of Safety and Allowable Stress: A factor of safety compares a material or component limit with the design demand under stated failure criteria.
topics.title: Factor of Safety and Allowable Stress

topics.summary: Fatigue: Endurance Limit and the Goodman Line: Cyclic loads fail parts far below yield; the endurance limit bounds infinite life for fully reversed stress, and the Goodman line extends that bound to mean-stress reality.
topics.title: Fatigue: Endurance Limit and the Goodman Line

topics.summary: Bolted Joints: Preload and Load Sharing: A properly preloaded bolted joint makes the clamped members absorb most of the external load - the bolt only feels the stiffness fraction, and the joint never separates.
topics.title: Bolted Joints: Preload and Load Sharing

topics.summary: Shaft Critical Speed and Lateral Vibration: A rotating shaft has a natural frequency of lateral vibration; running near it magnifies deflection without limit, so the operating speed is kept well away from the critical.
topics.title: Shaft Critical Speed and Lateral Vibration

subjects.description: Conduction, convection, radiation and heat exchanger design.
subjects.name: Heat & Mass Transfer

topics.summary: Heat flow through a solid is proportional to area and to the temperature gradient.
topics.title: Fourier's law of conduction

topics.summary: Convection: Newton's Law of Cooling and the Nusselt Number: Convective heat flow is a coefficient times area times temperature difference - and the Nusselt number reports how much the moving fluid multiplies plain conduction.
topics.title: Convection: Newton's Law of Cooling and the Nusselt Number

topics.summary: Thermal Radiation: Stefan-Boltzmann Exchange: Every surface radiates with the fourth power of its absolute temperature, and net exchange between surfaces is the difference of those fourth powers, trimmed by emissivity.
topics.title: Thermal Radiation: Stefan-Boltzmann Exchange

topics.summary: Log-Mean Temperature Difference and Exchanger Duty: A heat exchanger's duty is its overall conductance times area times a mean temperature difference, and the logarithmic mean is the number that correctly averages the two ends of the exchanger.
topics.title: Log-Mean Temperature Difference and Exchanger Duty

subjects.description: Kinematics of mechanisms, gears, cams, governors and balancing.
subjects.name: Theory of Machines

topics.summary: Gear Ratio and Rotational Speed: For an ideal external gear pair, tooth-count ratio sets the inverse speed ratio and reverses rotation direction.
topics.title: Gear Ratio and Rotational Speed

topics.summary: Four-Bar Linkages and Grashof's Criterion: Whether a four-bar linkage can rotate a link fully depends on one length inequality - Grashof's condition - and which link is grounded decides the mechanism's personality.
topics.title: Four-Bar Linkages and Grashof's Criterion

topics.summary: Flywheels: Energy Fluctuation and Coefficient of Fluctuation: A flywheel is rotational energy storage that smooths a machine's speed: its inertia absorbs the cycle's energy surplus and returns the deficit within a narrow speed band.
topics.title: Flywheels: Energy Fluctuation and Coefficient of Fluctuation

topics.summary: Compound Gear Trains: Ratio, Torque and the Cost of Each Stage: A compound train multiplies ratios and loses a little power in every mesh, so the output speed and torque follow from the product of the stages and their efficiencies.
topics.title: Compound Gear Trains: Ratio, Torque and the Cost of Each Stage

subjects.description: SI/CI cycles, fuel systems, emissions and engine performance.
subjects.name: Internal Combustion Engines

topics.summary: Brake Thermal Efficiency of an Engine: Brake thermal efficiency compares useful shaft power with the chemical energy rate entering in the fuel.
topics.title: Brake Thermal Efficiency of an Engine

topics.summary: Air-Fuel Ratio and Combustion Stoichiometry: Complete combustion has an exact chemical recipe; the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio follows from balancing the reaction, and real engines run rich or lean against it deliberately.
topics.title: Air-Fuel Ratio and Combustion Stoichiometry

topics.summary: Engine Performance Maps: BSFC and the Torque-Power Curve: Power is torque times speed, but efficiency is brake-specific fuel consumption - and the BSFC map shows the small island where an engine actually earns its fuel.
topics.title: Engine Performance Maps: BSFC and the Torque-Power Curve

topics.summary: Volumetric Efficiency, Airflow and Fuel Flow: An engine's power follows its airflow, and airflow is swept volume times density times volumetric efficiency - so boost, speed and breathing are the only levers.
topics.title: Volumetric Efficiency, Airflow and Fuel Flow

subjects.description: Parametric modelling, assembly design and CNC programming.
subjects.name: CAD / CAM

topics.summary: CAD/CAM: From Parametric Model to Verified Toolpath: A parametric CAD model expresses design intent; CAM transforms a checked part model and setup into a machine-specific toolpath.
topics.title: CAD/CAM: From Parametric Model to Verified Toolpath

topics.summary: Affine Transformations for Model Manipulation: Moving, scaling and rotating a CAD model is matrix multiplication on every point - and homogeneous coordinates make even translation fit the same multiplication.
topics.title: Affine Transformations for Model Manipulation

topics.summary: CNC Interpolation: Linear and Circular Toolpaths: An interpolator turns a programmed path and feed rate into synchronized axis commands, so the tool tip traces the geometry at exactly the surface speed the process needs.
topics.title: CNC Interpolation: Linear and Circular Toolpaths

topics.summary: Toolpath Step-Over, Scallop Height and Machining Time: A CAM toolpath is a set of trades: feed rate buys cycle time, step-over buys surface finish, and the cusp left between passes can be predicted before the part is cut.
topics.title: Toolpath Step-Over, Scallop Height and Machining Time

subjects.description: Vapour compression cycles, psychrometrics and system design.
subjects.name: Refrigeration & Air Conditioning

topics.summary: Vapour-Compression Refrigeration COP: The coefficient of performance measures heat removed from the cold space per unit work supplied to the cycle.
topics.title: Vapour-Compression Refrigeration COP

topics.summary: Psychrometrics: Humidity Ratio and Comfort Cooling: Moist air behaves as a mixture whose water content is tracked by the humidity ratio, and comfort cooling is as much a dehumidification problem as a temperature one.
topics.title: Psychrometrics: Humidity Ratio and Comfort Cooling

topics.summary: Cooling Load and Sensible Heat Ratio: A space's cooling duty splits into temperature-changing sensible load and moisture-removing latent load, and their ratio must match the coil's own ratio or comfort fails.
topics.title: Cooling Load and Sensible Heat Ratio

topics.summary: Refrigeration COP and the Condenser Temperature Penalty: A vapour-compression cycle's efficiency is bounded by the Carnot limit between its two temperatures, and the condenser temperature costs more than the evaporator temperature is worth.
topics.title: Refrigeration COP and the Condenser Temperature Penalty

subjects.description: Semiconductor physics, diodes, BJTs, FETs and amplifiers.
subjects.name: Electronic Devices & Circuits

topics.summary: Diode I–V Behaviour and Load-Line Checks: A diode's current changes nonlinearly with junction voltage; a series resistor and source establish the operating point.
topics.title: Diode I–V Behaviour and Load-Line Checks

topics.summary: MOSFET Operating Regions: Cut-Off, Triode and Saturation: One gate-voltage inequality chain decides whether a MOSFET is an open switch, a voltage-controlled resistor, or a current source - and analog and digital design live in different regions on purpose.
topics.title: MOSFET Operating Regions: Cut-Off, Triode and Saturation

topics.summary: Carrier Transport: Drift and Diffusion Currents: Current in a semiconductor flows two ways - carriers pushed by an electric field and carriers spreading down their own concentration gradient - and junctions run on both at once.
topics.title: Carrier Transport: Drift and Diffusion Currents

topics.summary: Small-Signal Transconductance and Stage Gain: A bipolar transistor's small-signal behaviour is one number: the transconductance, which is the collector current divided by the thermal voltage, and it sets the gain an amplifier can deliver.
topics.title: Small-Signal Transconductance and Stage Gain

subjects.description: Boolean algebra, logic families, combinational and sequential design.
subjects.name: Digital Electronics

topics.summary: Simplifying logic expressions so circuits need fewer gates - the manual version of what synthesis tools automate.
topics.title: Boolean Algebra & Karnaugh Maps

topics.summary: Logic Families: Noise Margin and Fan-Out: Two voltage windows and two current budgets decide whether one gate's output can be another gate's reliable input - noise margin for voltage, fan-out for current.
topics.title: Logic Families: Noise Margin and Fan-Out

topics.summary: Counters: Ripple versus Synchronous and Modulus Design: A counter is flip-flops plus steering logic; ripple counters pay delay per stage while synchronous counters pay it once - and the modulus decides how many stages are needed.
topics.title: Counters: Ripple versus Synchronous and Modulus Design

topics.summary: Setup and Hold Slack in a Synchronous Path: Timing closure is arithmetic on one path: the clock period must exceed the total delay around the launch-flop-to-capture-flop path, and the hold check must pass no matter how fast the logic is.
topics.title: Setup and Hold Slack in a Synchronous Path

subjects.description: Convolution, Fourier, Laplace and Z transforms - the maths of signals.
subjects.name: Signals & Systems

topics.summary: The single operation that completely characterises any linear time-invariant system.
topics.title: Convolution & LTI Systems

topics.summary: Poles, Zeros and Stability in the s-Plane: A transfer function's pole locations are the system's natural behaviours: real parts set decay or growth, imaginary parts set oscillation, and the left half-plane is the border of stability.
topics.title: Poles, Zeros and Stability in the s-Plane

topics.summary: Frequency Response and Bode Plot Asymptotes: A Bode plot sketches gain and phase against frequency with straight-line rules: every pole bends the gain down 20 dB per decade at its corner frequency.
topics.title: Frequency Response and Bode Plot Asymptotes

topics.summary: Sampling-Rate Choice and the Anti-Aliasing Filter Order: The sampling rate and the anti-aliasing filter are one design: oversampling pushes the first alias band further away, which is what makes a practical analogue filter possible.
topics.title: Sampling-Rate Choice and the Anti-Aliasing Filter Order

subjects.description: AM/FM, digital modulation, noise, sampling and information theory.
subjects.name: Communication Systems

topics.summary: Shannon Capacity and the SNR Limit: Channel capacity bounds the error-free information rate for an ideal band-limited channel with additive white Gaussian noise.
topics.title: Shannon Capacity and the SNR Limit

topics.summary: Amplitude Modulation: Sidebands and Transmitted Power: AM carries information by letting the message scale a carrier's amplitude, and the power bookkeeping shows why the scheme is wasteful: most energy ships in the information-free carrier.
topics.title: Amplitude Modulation: Sidebands and Transmitted Power

topics.summary: PCM Quantization Noise and the 6-dB-per-Bit Rule: Digitizing an analog signal trades noise for bits in a fixed exchange rate: every added quantization bit buys about 6 dB of signal-to-quantization-noise ratio.
topics.title: PCM Quantization Noise and the 6-dB-per-Bit Rule

topics.summary: Link Budgets and Free-Space Path Loss: A radio link closes when the received power exceeds the receiver's sensitivity; free-space path loss plus a link budget is the arithmetic that answers whether it does.
topics.title: Link Budgets and Free-Space Path Loss

subjects.description: 8085/8086, ARM, assembly, interrupts and peripheral interfacing.
subjects.name: Microprocessors & Microcontrollers

topics.summary: Address Width and Memory-Mapped Peripherals: An n-bit byte-addressed address field can name at most 2ⁿ distinct byte locations before reserved regions and mapping are considered.
topics.title: Address Width and Memory-Mapped Peripherals

topics.summary: Interrupts: Latency, Priorities and ISR Design: An interrupt is the processor's doorbell for asynchronous events: it bounds reaction time to roughly one instruction, and priority logic decides which doorbell wins when several ring.
topics.title: Interrupts: Latency, Priorities and ISR Design

topics.summary: Timer Programming and Baud-Rate Generation: Microcontroller timers turn the system clock into measurable time by counting divided ticks, and serial baud rates are generated by choosing the divisor that makes one bit last exactly the right length.
topics.title: Timer Programming and Baud-Rate Generation

topics.summary: Timer Reload Values, PWM Resolution and Their Trade: A hardware timer turns a clock into a controlled period and duty; the reload value, the prescaler and the duty resolution cannot all be chosen freely, and that constraint is arithmetic.
topics.title: Timer Reload Values, PWM Resolution and Their Trade

subjects.description: Maxwell's equations, waves, transmission lines and radiation.
subjects.name: Electromagnetic Fields

topics.summary: Four equations that unify electricity, magnetism and light - the foundation of all electromagnetics.
topics.title: Maxwell's Equations

topics.summary: Gauss's Law Applied: Fields from Symmetric Charge: When charge distribution has enough symmetry, Gauss's law turns a hard integral into an algebra problem: flux out equals charge enclosed, and symmetry says the field is constant on the Gaussian surface you choose.
topics.title: Gauss's Law Applied: Fields from Symmetric Charge

topics.summary: Skin Depth and High-Frequency Conduction: AC current crowds toward a conductor's surface, and the skin depth formula says how deep it penetrates - the reason high-frequency resistance rises with sqrt(frequency).
topics.title: Skin Depth and High-Frequency Conduction

topics.summary: Reflection, Standing Waves and Impedance Matching: Whenever a guided wave meets an impedance change, part of it reflects back; the reflection coefficient and the standing-wave ratio quantify the mismatch and tell you what matching will buy.
topics.title: Reflection, Standing Waves and Impedance Matching

subjects.description: Amplifiers, feedback, oscillators and op-amp applications.
subjects.name: Analog Circuits

topics.summary: Non-Inverting Op-Amp Gain: With negative feedback and an ideal op amp, the non-inverting closed-loop gain is set by the resistor ratio.
topics.title: Non-Inverting Op-Amp Gain

topics.summary: Op-Amp Gain-Bandwidth Product: An op-amp's open-loop gain rolls off at 20 dB per decade, so gain times bandwidth stays fixed - choose closed-loop gain and the amplifier hands you the matching bandwidth.
topics.title: Op-Amp Gain-Bandwidth Product

topics.summary: Negative Feedback: Gain Desensitization and Its Price: Feeding a fraction of the output back in opposition trades raw gain for precision: the closed-loop gain stops depending on the amplifier and starts depending on the feedback network.
topics.title: Negative Feedback: Gain Desensitization and Its Price

topics.summary: Active Filters: Cutoff, Quality Factor and the Op-Amp's Bandwidth Bill: A second-order active filter is designed by two numbers - cutoff frequency and quality factor - and both are limited in practice by the amplifier's gain-bandwidth product.
topics.title: Active Filters: Cutoff, Quality Factor and the Op-Amp's Bandwidth Bill

subjects.description: Transfer functions, stability, root locus, Bode and state space.
subjects.name: Control Systems Engineering

topics.summary: First-Order Step Response and Time Constant: A stable first-order system reaches about 63.2% of a step change after one time constant.
topics.title: First-Order Step Response and Time Constant

topics.summary: Second-Order Step Response: Damping Ratio and Overshoot: Two numbers - natural frequency and damping ratio - predict the entire step response: how fast it rises, how much it overshoots, and how long it rings.
topics.title: Second-Order Step Response: Damping Ratio and Overshoot

topics.summary: Routh-Hurwitz Stability Criterion: The Routh array counts right-half-plane poles from the characteristic polynomial's coefficients alone - no root solving, and it answers 'for which gains is the system stable?' directly.
topics.title: Routh-Hurwitz Stability Criterion

topics.summary: Steady-State Error, System Type and the Final Value Theorem: How well a closed loop tracks a command is decided by the number of free integrators in its loop: type zero lags a step, type one lags a ramp, and the error is a number you can compute before the loop is built.
topics.title: Steady-State Error, System Type and the Final Value Theorem

subjects.description: DFT/FFT, filter design and multirate processing.
subjects.name: Digital Signal Processing

topics.summary: Sampling and the Nyquist Criterion: A band-limited signal needs a sampling rate greater than twice its highest frequency to avoid ideal aliasing.
topics.title: Sampling and the Nyquist Criterion

topics.summary: DFT and FFT Compute Cost: The DFT's direct evaluation costs N^2 operations while the FFT reuses symmetry to cost N log N - a difference that decides what real-time signal processing is possible.
topics.title: DFT and FFT Compute Cost

topics.summary: FIR versus IIR Filters: Stability and Phase Trade-Offs: FIR filters buy guaranteed stability and exact linear phase with taps; IIR filters buy sharp cutoffs with poles - and the choice is which property the application cannot lose.
topics.title: FIR versus IIR Filters: Stability and Phase Trade-Offs

topics.summary: FIR Filter Length from the Transition Width: A linear-phase FIR filter's cost is decided by its transition width: halving the width doubles the number of taps, and the tap count is the arithmetic load you must budget for.
topics.title: FIR Filter Length from the Transition Width

subjects.description: CMOS logic, layout, timing analysis and the digital design flow.
subjects.name: VLSI Design

topics.summary: Dynamic Power in CMOS Logic: CMOS dynamic power grows with switched capacitance, the square of supply voltage, clock frequency, and activity.
topics.title: Dynamic Power in CMOS Logic

topics.summary: CMOS Inverter Switching Threshold and Noise Margins: The inverter's switching point is where both transistors saturate and their currents match; sizing the pair sets that point, and the transfer curve's shape sets the noise margins.
topics.title: CMOS Inverter Switching Threshold and Noise Margins

topics.summary: Interconnect Delay: Elmore Delay and RC Trees: Once wires stopped being ideal, gate delay stopped being the whole story: the Elmore delay of an RC tree estimates signal arrival with one first-moment sum.
topics.title: Interconnect Delay: Elmore Delay and RC Trees

topics.summary: Dynamic Power, Voltage Scaling and Energy per Operation: A digital block's power is activity times capacitance times voltage squared times frequency, which is why voltage scaling is the strongest energy lever available and why it slows the circuit down.
topics.title: Dynamic Power, Voltage Scaling and Energy per Operation

subjects.description: Network analysis, theorems, transients and two-port networks.
subjects.name: Circuit Theory

topics.summary: The two conservation rules - charge and energy - that let you solve any circuit.
topics.title: Kirchhoff's Laws

topics.summary: Thevenin and Norton Equivalents: Any two-terminal linear network collapses to one voltage source with one series resistance - or one current source with one parallel resistance - and every load question gets simpler.
topics.title: Thevenin and Norton Equivalents

topics.summary: Maximum Power Transfer and Its 50% Efficiency: A source delivers peak power to a load exactly when the load resistance mirrors the source's internal resistance - and that condition wastes half the power by construction.
topics.title: Maximum Power Transfer and Its 50% Efficiency

topics.summary: Measurement-Derived Thevenin Equivalents and Maximum Power Transfer: Any linear two-terminal network looks like one voltage source and one resistance; two measurements find both, and the resulting pair decides what load extracts the most power.
topics.title: Measurement-Derived Thevenin Equivalents and Maximum Power Transfer

subjects.description: Transformers and DC machines: construction, characteristics, testing.
subjects.name: Electrical Machines I

topics.summary: Transferring electrical power between circuits at different voltages using a shared magnetic field.
topics.title: Transformers

topics.summary: Transformer Efficiency and Voltage Regulation: A transformer's two loss families - fixed core loss and load-squared copper loss - set both its efficiency curve and the voltage sag its terminals show from no-load to full-load.
topics.title: Transformer Efficiency and Voltage Regulation

topics.summary: EMF Equation of DC Machines: One equation links flux, speed and winding layout to the generated voltage - and the same expression, with current instead of voltage, gives the torque.
topics.title: EMF Equation of DC Machines

topics.summary: DC Machine Speed, Back EMF and Field Weakening: A DC machine's speed follows its back-EMF law: at fixed field, speed falls with armature drop, and weakening the field raises speed at the cost of torque.
topics.title: DC Machine Speed, Back EMF and Field Weakening

subjects.description: Induction and synchronous machines, torque and performance.
subjects.name: Electrical Machines II

topics.summary: Induction-Motor Slip and Rotor Speed: Slip measures the fractional difference between synchronous field speed and rotor speed in an induction motor.
topics.title: Induction-Motor Slip and Rotor Speed

topics.summary: Synchronous Generator EMF and Voltage Regulation: A synchronous machine's generated voltage is set by flux, frequency and winding layout through the 4.44 law - and its terminal voltage under load falls by the synchronous-impedance drop.
topics.title: Synchronous Generator EMF and Voltage Regulation

topics.summary: Induction Motor Starting and V/f Speed Control: An induction motor's flux lives in the ratio of voltage to frequency: hold V/f constant and the torque capability survives a speed change - which is the entire principle of inverter drives.
topics.title: Induction Motor Starting and V/f Speed Control

topics.summary: Reduced-Voltage Starting of Induction Motors: A large induction motor draws several times its rated current at standstill, so starting methods trade current against torque; the trade is a squared ratio that can be computed in advance.
topics.title: Reduced-Voltage Starting of Induction Motors

subjects.description: Generation, transmission lines, load flow, faults and protection.
subjects.name: Power Systems

topics.summary: Normalising power system quantities so machines of different ratings can be compared directly.
topics.title: Per-Unit System & Fault Analysis

topics.summary: Power-Angle Equation and Transmission Limits: Real power across a transmission link is a sine of the angle between the two end voltages, and that curve sets both the steady transfer limit and the stability story.
topics.title: Power-Angle Equation and Transmission Limits

topics.summary: Economic Dispatch and Incremental Cost: The cheapest way to meet a load is to run every online generator at the same incremental cost - equal slopes of the cost curves, not equal outputs.
topics.title: Economic Dispatch and Incremental Cost

topics.summary: Voltage Drop and Losses on a Distribution Feeder: Line drop and line loss are two different numbers: the first decides whether customers get the right voltage, the second decides what the utility pays, and both follow from the same current and impedance.
topics.title: Voltage Drop and Losses on a Distribution Feeder

subjects.description: Rectifiers, choppers, inverters and converter control.
subjects.name: Power Electronics

topics.summary: Ideal Buck Converter Duty Ratio: In continuous-conduction ideal operation, a buck converter's average output voltage is duty ratio times input voltage.
topics.title: Ideal Buck Converter Duty Ratio

topics.summary: Controlled Rectifiers: Firing Angle and Average Output: Delaying each thyristor's turn-on by the firing angle chops the waveform's front and lowers the average output predictably - the cosine law of phase control.
topics.title: Controlled Rectifiers: Firing Angle and Average Output

topics.summary: PWM Inverters: Modulation Index and Fundamental Control: A PWM inverter chops a DC rail at high frequency, and the ratio of modulating to carrier amplitude - the modulation index - linearly sets the fundamental output voltage.
topics.title: PWM Inverters: Modulation Index and Fundamental Control

topics.summary: Boost Converter Design: Duty, Inductor Ripple and Output Ripple: A boost converter's duty ratio sets its voltage ratio, its inductor sets the current ripple and its capacitor sets the output ripple - three numbers that can be chosen independently.
topics.title: Boost Converter Design: Duty, Inductor Ripple and Output Ripple

subjects.description: Bridges, transducers, CROs and measurement error analysis.
subjects.name: Measurements & Instrumentation

topics.summary: Calibration Error and Measurement Uncertainty: Measurement error compares a reading with a reference; uncertainty describes the range of values reasonably attributable to the measurand.
topics.title: Calibration Error and Measurement Uncertainty

topics.summary: Wheatstone Bridge and Null Measurement: A bridge measures an unknown resistance by balancing two divider ratios to zero output - and null measurement wins because the detector reads zero, not a calibrated scale.
topics.title: Wheatstone Bridge and Null Measurement

topics.summary: Strain Gauges and Gauge Factor: A strain gauge converts deformation into resistance change, and the gauge factor is the sensitivity constant that turns ohms into microstrain.
topics.title: Strain Gauges and Gauge Factor

topics.summary: Error Propagation in a Derived Measurement: A computed quantity inherits the errors of its inputs, and the size of the inherited error depends on how the inputs are combined - which tells you which instrument to buy next.
topics.title: Error Propagation in a Derived Measurement

subjects.description: Chain, compass, levelling, theodolite and modern total stations.
subjects.name: Surveying

topics.summary: Backsights and foresights turn staff readings into a height difference.
topics.title: Differential leveling

topics.summary: Traversing: Latitude, Departure and Bowditch Balancing: A closed traverse must return to its start, so the latitudes and departures of all legs must sum to zero - and the residual error is distributed by a defined rule, not hidden.
topics.title: Traversing: Latitude, Departure and Bowditch Balancing

topics.summary: Contours: Interval, Gradient and Interpolation: Contour lines are the terrain's level curves, and their spacing on a map is an inverse reading of slope - dense means steep, with the interval setting the scale of legibility.
topics.title: Contours: Interval, Gradient and Interpolation

topics.summary: Reciprocal Levelling and the Curvature Correction: Two instrument setups across a river separate the true level difference from the instrument's own collimation error, and the curvature and refraction correction quantifies what the Earth's surface does to a level line.
topics.title: Reciprocal Levelling and the Curvature Correction

subjects.description: Determinacy, moment distribution, slope-deflection and influence lines.
subjects.name: Structural Analysis

topics.summary: Equilibrium and Structural Determinacy: A planar structure at rest must satisfy force and moment equilibrium; equilibrium alone does not guarantee stability or code adequacy.
topics.title: Equilibrium and Structural Determinacy

topics.summary: Shear and Bending Moment Diagrams for Beams: Load, shear and moment are derivatives of one another, so each diagram is the integral of the last - and the peak moment lives where shear crosses zero.
topics.title: Shear and Bending Moment Diagrams for Beams

topics.summary: Truss Analysis: Method of Sections: Cutting a truss through three members exposes their forces directly from three equilibrium equations - the shortcut when only one member's force is wanted.
topics.title: Truss Analysis: Method of Sections

topics.summary: Moment Distribution: Distribution Factors and Carry-Over: Hardy Cross's method finds indeterminate moments by releasing one joint at a time, and its two numbers - the distribution factor and the carry-over half - make the iteration mechanical.
topics.title: Moment Distribution: Distribution Factors and Carry-Over

subjects.description: Cement chemistry, mix design, workability, strength and durability.
subjects.name: Concrete Technology

topics.summary: Choosing proportions so fresh concrete can be placed and hardened concrete reaches its design strength.
topics.title: Concrete Mix Design & Workability

topics.summary: Water-Cement Ratio and Abram's Law: Concrete strength is governed less by cement brand than by one ratio - water to cement - and Abram's law quantifies the exponential penalty for every extra litre.
topics.title: Water-Cement Ratio and Abram's Law

topics.summary: Creep, Shrinkage and Durability Cover: Concrete keeps deforming long after it hardens - creep under load, shrinkage as it dries - and the cover depth decides how long the reinforcement survives the environment.
topics.title: Creep, Shrinkage and Durability Cover

topics.summary: Modulus of Elasticity and the Stiffness of Concrete: Concrete's modulus can be estimated from its strength grade, which links a mix design decision to the deflection of the finished member.
topics.title: Modulus of Elasticity and the Stiffness of Concrete

subjects.description: Index properties, permeability, consolidation, shear strength and bearing capacity.
subjects.name: Soil Mechanics / Geotechnical Engineering

topics.summary: Why water in soil controls whether a foundation stands or sinks.
topics.title: Effective Stress & Bearing Capacity

topics.summary: Consolidation: Time Factor and Settlement Rate: Clay settles as water squeezes out, and Terzaghi's time factor says how long that takes - proportional to the square of the drainage path, which is why drains accelerate it.
topics.title: Consolidation: Time Factor and Settlement Rate

topics.summary: Soil Compaction: Optimum Moisture Content and Field Density: Every soil has a moisture content at which a given compactive effort packs it densest; field acceptance is measured as a percentage of that laboratory maximum.
topics.title: Soil Compaction: Optimum Moisture Content and Field Density
