topics.summary: Rankine Earth Pressure and the Effect of Water Behind a Wall: A retaining wall is designed against the lateral thrust of the soil behind it, and if that soil is saturated the water pressure can exceed the soil's own contribution.
topics.title: Rankine Earth Pressure and the Effect of Water Behind a Wall

subjects.description: Limit state design of beams, slabs, columns and footings.
subjects.name: Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures

topics.summary: Flexural Resistance of a Reinforced-Concrete Beam: A singly reinforced beam resists bending through a compression block in concrete and tension carried mainly by steel reinforcement.
topics.title: Flexural Resistance of a Reinforced-Concrete Beam

topics.summary: Shear Design of RC Beams and Stirrup Spacing: Concrete carries part of the shear; stirrups carry the rest - and their spacing follows directly from how much shear force the steel must intercept on each potential crack.
topics.title: Shear Design of RC Beams and Stirrup Spacing

topics.summary: Limit State Design: Partial Safety Factors: Limit-state design separates what might happen (factored loads) from what material actually delivers (divided strengths), so a single inequality guarantees a target reliability.
topics.title: Limit State Design: Partial Safety Factors

topics.summary: Development Length and Anchorage of Reinforcement: A bar must be embedded long enough for the bond between steel and concrete to develop the force in it, and that length scales with bar diameter and stress.
topics.title: Development Length and Anchorage of Reinforcement

subjects.description: Open channel flow, pipes, pumps and turbines.
subjects.name: Hydraulics & Hydraulic Machinery

topics.summary: Pump Hydraulic Power and Head: Hydraulic power is the rate of potential energy delivered to a fluid flow; shaft input is larger by the inverse of pump efficiency.
topics.title: Pump Hydraulic Power and Head

topics.summary: Open-Channel Flow: Manning's Equation: Gravity drives open-channel flow, and Manning's equation ties depth, slope and surface roughness to velocity through the hydraulic radius - the workhorse of drain, canal and sewer design.
topics.title: Open-Channel Flow: Manning's Equation

topics.summary: Hydraulic Jump and Specific Energy: A supercritical flow can return to subcritical only through a hydraulic jump - an abrupt, energy-destroying transition whose conjugate depths follow from momentum, not energy.
topics.title: Hydraulic Jump and Specific Energy

topics.summary: Pump Affinity Laws and Speed Control: Changing a pump's speed moves its whole characteristic: flow in proportion, head with the square and power with the cube - which is why speed control saves energy that throttling wastes.
topics.title: Pump Affinity Laws and Speed Control

subjects.description: Highway alignment, pavement design and traffic engineering.
subjects.name: Transportation Engineering

topics.summary: Stopping Sight Distance: Stopping sight distance combines distance traveled during perception-reaction time with braking distance under a stated road condition.
topics.title: Stopping Sight Distance

topics.summary: Superelevation and Horizontal Curve Design: On a curve, banking the pavement supplies part of the centripetal demand and friction supplies the rest - the design equation budgets the two against each other.
topics.title: Superelevation and Horizontal Curve Design

topics.summary: Traffic Flow Fundamentals: Speed, Flow and Density: Flow equals density times speed - one identity whose curve against density explains capacity, congestion and why adding demand past a point destroys throughput.
topics.title: Traffic Flow Fundamentals: Speed, Flow and Density

topics.summary: Equivalent Standard Axles and Pavement Load Accumulation: Pavement damage grows roughly with the fourth power of axle load, so one heavy vehicle can be worth thousands of cars and the design traffic is counted in equivalent standard axles.
topics.title: Equivalent Standard Axles and Pavement Load Accumulation

subjects.description: Water supply, wastewater treatment and solid waste management.
subjects.name: Environmental Engineering

topics.summary: Wastewater Treatment Removal Efficiency: Removal efficiency compares influent and effluent concentration for one stated contaminant and treatment boundary.
topics.title: Wastewater Treatment Removal Efficiency

topics.summary: Water Demand Estimation and Population Forecasting: A water system is sized for a future population, not today's: geometric growth plus per-capita demand sets the design discharge that every downstream unit must carry.
topics.title: Water Demand Estimation and Population Forecasting

topics.summary: Activated Sludge: Food-to-Microorganism Ratio: The aeration tank is a managed microbial ecosystem, and F/M - the daily BOD load per kilogram of biomass - is the dial that sets treatment efficiency, sludge production and oxygen demand.
topics.title: Activated Sludge: Food-to-Microorganism Ratio

topics.summary: Gaussian Plume Dispersion and Stack Height: The ground-level concentration from a stack falls rapidly as the effective stack height rises, which is why stack height and buoyancy are the strongest controls on local air quality.
topics.title: Gaussian Plume Dispersion and Stack Height

subjects.description: Quantity take-off, rate analysis, tendering and contracts.
subjects.name: Estimating & Costing

topics.summary: Quantity Take-Off and Rate Analysis: A measured work item is costed by multiplying its verified quantity by an applicable unit rate, then adding explicit indirect costs and taxes.
topics.title: Quantity Take-Off and Rate Analysis

topics.summary: Bar Bending Schedules and Reinforcement Quantities: A bar bending schedule turns a structural drawing into cut lengths, bends and kilograms of steel - the document the bar-bending shop builds from and the bill pays against.
topics.title: Bar Bending Schedules and Reinforcement Quantities

topics.summary: Earthwork Volumes: Trapezoidal and Prismoidal Rules: Longitudinal earthwork volumes come from cross-section areas at intervals, and the rule chosen to interpolate between them shifts the answer - and the payment - by several percent.
topics.title: Earthwork Volumes: Trapezoidal and Prismoidal Rules

topics.summary: Rate Analysis: Building Up a Unit Rate with Overheads and Profit: A tender rate is built from measured quantities, current prices and explicit factors for overheads, profit and waste - and every one of those factors is visible in the arithmetic.
topics.title: Rate Analysis: Building Up a Unit Rate with Overheads and Profit

subjects.description: Material and energy balances - the accountant's skill of chemical engineering.
subjects.name: Process Calculations

topics.summary: The accountant's discipline of chemical engineering: what goes in must come out or accumulate.
topics.title: Material & Energy Balances

topics.summary: Recycle, Bypass and Purge Balances: Recycle loops make balances iterative on purpose: what leaves unreacted comes back to the reactor, and the steady-state balance closes only when accumulation around the loop is zero.
topics.title: Recycle, Bypass and Purge Balances

topics.summary: Combustion Calculations: Theoretical and Excess Air: Combustion balancing fixes the exact air a fuel needs, and the excess-air percentage - readable from flue-gas oxygen - is the furnace's efficiency dial.
topics.title: Combustion Calculations: Theoretical and Excess Air

topics.summary: Recycle, Overall Conversion and the Law of Diminishing Returns: A recycle loop raises overall conversion beyond what one pass achieves, but the improvement saturates: each further increment of recycle buys less and costs more circulation.
topics.title: Recycle, Overall Conversion and the Law of Diminishing Returns

subjects.description: PVT behaviour, property relations, fugacity and equilibrium.
subjects.name: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics

topics.summary: Gibbs Free Energy and Reaction Direction: At constant temperature and pressure, Gibbs free-energy change indicates the thermodynamic driving direction for a process.
topics.title: Gibbs Free Energy and Reaction Direction

topics.summary: Clausius-Clapeyron Equation and Vapour Pressure: Vapour pressure rises exponentially with temperature, and the Clausius-Clapeyron relation quantifies the climb from one known point plus the heat of vaporization.
topics.title: Clausius-Clapeyron Equation and Vapour Pressure

topics.summary: van 't Hoff Equation and the Equilibrium Constant: Temperature moves chemical equilibrium in the direction Le Chatelier described, and van 't Hoff's equation is that principle with numbers: the sign of the reaction enthalpy decides the direction.
topics.title: van 't Hoff Equation and the Equilibrium Constant

topics.summary: Relative Volatility and Minimum Stages in Distillation: The ease of a distillation separation is captured by relative volatility, and the minimum number of theoretical stages needed follows from it by a single logarithm.
topics.title: Relative Volatility and Minimum Stages in Distillation

subjects.description: Flow through pipes, pumps, fluidisation and dimensional analysis.
subjects.name: Fluid Flow Operations

topics.summary: Reynolds Number and Flow Regime: The Reynolds number compares inertial and viscous effects and helps identify the flow regime in a specified geometry.
topics.title: Reynolds Number and Flow Regime

topics.summary: Packed-Bed Pressure Drop: The Ergun Equation: Flow through a bed of particles loses head to viscous drag at low speed and to form drag at high speed, and the Ergun equation is the sum of both regimes with the bed's geometry folded in.
topics.title: Packed-Bed Pressure Drop: The Ergun Equation

topics.summary: Flow Measurement: Orifice Meters and Discharge Coefficients: An orifice converts flow into a pressure difference through Bernoulli's constriction trick, and the discharge coefficient carries all the real-fluid corrections the ideal analysis misses.
topics.title: Flow Measurement: Orifice Meters and Discharge Coefficients

topics.summary: Pump Power, NPSH Available and Cavitation Margin: A pump needs both enough head and enough suction pressure, and the suction side is where pumps fail: available net positive suction head must exceed what the impeller requires.
topics.title: Pump Power, NPSH Available and Cavitation Margin

subjects.description: Exchanger design, evaporation, condensation and boiling.
subjects.name: Heat Transfer Operations

topics.summary: Heat Exchanger Duty and Log-Mean Temperature Difference: For a steady exchanger with an approximately constant overall coefficient, duty is UA times the log-mean temperature difference.
topics.title: Heat Exchanger Duty and Log-Mean Temperature Difference

topics.summary: Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient and Fouling: A heat exchanger's duty runs through a stack of resistances - two films, a wall, and the fouling layers time adds - and the weakest resistance's opposite, the lowest h, dominates the total.
topics.title: Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient and Fouling

topics.summary: Evaporator Steam Economy and Multiple Effects: Evaporating water costs steam, and multiple-effect evaporation recycles each kilogram's latent heat across stages - the steam economy counts how many times it gets used.
topics.title: Evaporator Steam Economy and Multiple Effects

topics.summary: Fouling Resistance and the Controlling Heat Transfer Resistance: An overall coefficient is a sum of resistances in series, and the largest one controls both the duty and where any improvement effort should go.
topics.title: Fouling Resistance and the Controlling Heat Transfer Resistance

subjects.description: Diffusion, absorption, distillation, extraction and drying.
subjects.name: Mass Transfer Operations

topics.summary: Fick's Law and Diffusive Flux: For one-dimensional molecular diffusion in a simple medium, flux moves down the concentration gradient.
topics.title: Fick's Law and Diffusive Flux

topics.summary: Distillation: McCabe-Thiele Stages and Reflux Ratio: A distillation column is a staircase between an equilibrium curve and two operating lines, and the reflux ratio sets both the staircase's shape and the column's energy bill.
topics.title: Distillation: McCabe-Thiele Stages and Reflux Ratio

topics.summary: Absorption: Operating Lines and Minimum Liquid Rate: Scrubbing a solute out of a gas is a counter-current balance walk between an operating line and an equilibrium curve - and the liquid rate's floor is set by a pinch, not by chemistry.
topics.title: Absorption: Operating Lines and Minimum Liquid Rate

topics.summary: Two-Film Theory and the Overall Mass Transfer Coefficient: Gas absorption passes through two films in series, and the slope of the equilibrium line decides which film controls the rate - often not the one intuition suggests.
topics.title: Two-Film Theory and the Overall Mass Transfer Coefficient

subjects.description: Kinetics, reactor design, residence time and non-ideal flow.
subjects.name: Chemical Reaction Engineering

topics.summary: First-Order Batch-Reactor Conversion: For a constant-volume first-order batch reaction, concentration decays exponentially with elapsed reaction time.
topics.title: First-Order Batch-Reactor Conversion

topics.summary: PFR versus CSTR Sizing for First-Order Reactions: For the same conversion, a plug-flow reactor is always smaller than a back-mixed one - the CSTR runs entirely at its outlet's slow, low-concentration condition, while the PFR exploits the fast inlet.
topics.title: PFR versus CSTR Sizing for First-Order Reactions

topics.summary: Arrhenius Kinetics: Activation Energy and Temperature Sensitivity: Reaction rates climb exponentially with temperature, and the activation energy sets the steepness - high-Ea reactions are temperature levers, low-Ea ones are not.
topics.title: Arrhenius Kinetics: Activation Energy and Temperature Sensitivity

topics.summary: CSTR Volume for a Second-Order Reaction and the Cost of High Conversion: A well-mixed reactor always runs at the lowest concentration in the system, so the volume needed to reach high conversion with second-order kinetics grows very steeply.
topics.title: CSTR Volume for a Second-Order Reaction and the Cost of High Conversion

subjects.description: Crystal structure, defects, phase diagrams, mechanical behaviour and failure.
subjects.name: Materials Science & Engineering

topics.summary: Hall–Petch Strengthening and Grain Size: For many polycrystalline metals over a useful grain-size range, smaller grains impede dislocation motion and raise yield strength.
topics.title: Hall–Petch Strengthening and Grain Size

topics.summary: Eutectic Reactions and Reading Phase Diagrams: A phase diagram is a map of stable phases versus temperature and composition, and the eutectic point is its most important landmark: the lowest-melting composition, where one liquid freezes into two solids at once.
topics.title: Eutectic Reactions and Reading Phase Diagrams

topics.summary: Diffusion in Solids: Fick's Second Law and Carburizing: Atoms migrate through solids by thermally activated jumps, so diffusion depth grows with the square root of time - the law that sizes every heat-treatment soak.
topics.title: Diffusion in Solids: Fick's Second Law and Carburizing

topics.summary: Work Hardening and the Onset of Necking: A ductile metal gets stronger as it is deformed, and the point at which it starts to neck follows from the hardening exponent alone - which is why that exponent is quoted as a design property.
topics.title: Work Hardening and the Onset of Necking

subjects.description: Service objectives, observability, incident response, and reliability engineering.
subjects.name: Site Reliability Engineering

topics.summary: SLOs, SLIs, and Error Budgets: A service-level indicator measures user-visible behavior; an objective sets the target and the error budget makes reliability trade-offs explicit.
topics.title: SLOs, SLIs, and Error Budgets

topics.summary: MTBF, MTTR and Steady-State Availability: Availability is the fraction of time a system is up, and it decomposes into how often it fails (MTBF) and how fast you recover (MTTR) - both are engineering targets, not fate.
topics.title: MTBF, MTTR and Steady-State Availability

topics.summary: Monitoring: Golden Signals and Alert Thresholds: Four signals - latency, traffic, errors, saturation - describe every user-facing service, and alerting works when it fires on user-harm symptoms rather than internal causes.
topics.title: Monitoring: Golden Signals and Alert Thresholds

topics.summary: Error-Budget Burn Rate and Two-Window Alerting: A burn rate expresses how fast an error budget is being spent, which turns an SLO into an alerting rule: a short window catches fast burns, a longer window catches slow ones.
topics.title: Error-Budget Burn Rate and Two-Window Alerting

subjects.description: Consensus, transaction ordering, smart-contract safety, and distributed trust.
subjects.name: Distributed Ledger & Smart Contract Engineering

topics.summary: Hash-Linked Blocks and Transaction Integrity: A block header commits to its parent and transaction set; changing committed data changes the digest and breaks downstream links.
topics.title: Hash-Linked Blocks and Transaction Integrity

topics.summary: Merkle Trees and Efficient Transaction Proofs: A block commits to thousands of transactions with a single root hash, and a Merkle tree lets anyone verify one transaction's inclusion with only a logarithmic handful of hashes.
topics.title: Merkle Trees and Efficient Transaction Proofs

topics.summary: Consensus Trade-Offs: Fault Tolerance Bounds and Finality: Byzantine consensus needs more than two-thirds honest participation to certify anything, and 'final' means different things - probabilistic in Nakamoto chains, absolute in BFT voting.
topics.title: Consensus Trade-Offs: Fault Tolerance Bounds and Finality

topics.summary: Confirmations, Reorganisation Risk and the Safety Bound: Confirmation depth is a risk decision: the chance that a chain is replaced falls exponentially with depth for an attacker holding a minority of the mining or staking power.
topics.title: Confirmations, Reorganisation Risk and the Safety Bound

subjects.description: Sensors, embedded nodes, gateways, communication protocols, and device lifecycle.
subjects.name: Internet of Things Systems Design

topics.summary: Sensor Calibration and IoT Measurement Quality: A calibrated sensor maps a physical input to a reported value with a documented scale, offset, uncertainty, and operating range.
topics.title: Sensor Calibration and IoT Measurement Quality

topics.summary: Link Budgets and the Friis Transmission Equation: A radio link works when received power beats receiver sensitivity with margin, and the link budget adds and subtracts every gain and loss in decibels to prove it.
topics.title: Link Budgets and the Friis Transmission Equation

topics.summary: Duty Cycling and Battery Life Estimation: A battery-powered node lives on its average current, not its peak: sleeping microseconds and waking milliseconds blend into one number that sets months or years.
topics.title: Duty Cycling and Battery Life Estimation

topics.summary: ADC Resolution, Quantisation and Duty-Cycled Battery Life: Two numbers decide most IoT designs: the resolution of the measurement and the mean current the node draws, and both are simple arithmetic on the data sheet.
topics.title: ADC Resolution, Quantisation and Duty-Cycled Battery Life

subjects.description: Coordinate frames, forward kinematics, sensing, actuation, and feedback control.
subjects.name: Robotics Kinematics & Control

topics.summary: Forward Kinematics of a Two-Link Planar Arm: Forward kinematics maps joint angles and link lengths to the end-effector position in a chosen coordinate frame.
topics.title: Forward Kinematics of a Two-Link Planar Arm

topics.summary: Inverse Kinematics and Workspace Limits for a Planar Arm: Forward kinematics maps angles to a tip position; inverse kinematics runs it backwards - solving for the angles that reach a target, and refusing targets outside the workspace annulus.
topics.title: Inverse Kinematics and Workspace Limits for a Planar Arm

topics.summary: Trajectory Planning: Trapezoidal Velocity Profiles: Moving between two points fast without slamming the drives means shaping velocity as a trapezoid: ramp up within acceleration limits, cruise, ramp down.
topics.title: Trajectory Planning: Trapezoidal Velocity Profiles

topics.summary: The Jacobian, Singularities and Joint-Speed Demand: The Jacobian maps joint rates to end-effector velocity, and its determinant tells you when the arm loses a degree of freedom - and how much extra joint speed the remaining directions demand.
topics.title: The Jacobian, Singularities and Joint-Speed Demand

subjects.description: Integrating mechanical plants, sensors, control logic, and actuators into safe systems.
subjects.name: Mechatronic System Design

topics.summary: Closed-Loop Sensor, Controller, and Actuator Design: A mechatronic loop measures output, compares it with a reference, and drives an actuator to reduce the error.
topics.title: Closed-Loop Sensor, Controller, and Actuator Design

topics.summary: Stepper Motor Sizing: Torque Budget and Microstepping: A stepper must out-torque the sum of load, friction and its own acceleration demand with margin - and its torque collapses with speed, so the budget is checked at the fastest step rate, not standstill.
topics.title: Stepper Motor Sizing: Torque Budget and Microstepping

topics.summary: Sensor Fusion: Complementary Filtering Basics: A gyro knows fast changes but drifts; an accelerometer knows the horizon but vibrates - a complementary filter sums their strengths with one tunable constant.
topics.title: Sensor Fusion: Complementary Filtering Basics

topics.summary: Sampling Rate, Loop Delay and the Torque Budget: A closed-loop mechatronic design is bounded by two calculations: the sampling rate that keeps the digital loop behaving like the analogue one it replaces, and the torque the actuator must supply.
topics.title: Sampling Rate, Loop Delay and the Torque Budget

subjects.description: Demand planning, capacity, scheduling, inventory, and shop-floor control.
subjects.name: Production Planning & Control

topics.summary: Overall Equipment Effectiveness: OEE combines availability, performance, and quality to describe productive output relative to planned production time.
topics.title: Overall Equipment Effectiveness

topics.summary: Line Balancing: Takt Time and Workstation Count: A paced line must finish each unit within the takt - the heartbeat demand sets - and the theoretical station count is the total task time divided by that heartbeat.
topics.title: Line Balancing: Takt Time and Workstation Count

topics.summary: Little's Law: WIP, Throughput and Lead Time: In any steady flow system, work in process equals throughput times lead time - no assumptions about routing, variability or process detail, which is why the law is a management lever.
topics.title: Little's Law: WIP, Throughput and Lead Time

topics.summary: Capacity Requirements from Demand, Work Content and OEE: Capacity planning is arithmetic on three numbers: how much work a part needs, how many parts are wanted, and what fraction of the available time the equipment is actually productive.
topics.title: Capacity Requirements from Demand, Work Content and OEE

subjects.description: Linear programming, queues, inventory, and evidence-based systems optimization.
subjects.name: Operations Research & Optimization

topics.summary: Economic Order Quantity and Inventory Trade-Off: The basic EOQ model balances fixed ordering cost against inventory holding cost under steady, deterministic demand.
topics.title: Economic Order Quantity and Inventory Trade-Off

topics.summary: Linear Programming: Graphical Method and Corner-Point Optimality: A linear objective over linear constraints reaches its optimum at a corner of the feasible polygon - so solving a two-variable LP is drawing the region and pricing its vertices.
topics.title: Linear Programming: Graphical Method and Corner-Point Optimality

topics.summary: Critical Path Method and Project Float: A project's duration is its longest dependency chain, and every activity off that chain carries float - slack that scheduling software hides and schedulers must manage.
topics.title: Critical Path Method and Project Float

topics.summary: The Newsvendor Quantity and the Critical Ratio: When a decision must be made before demand is known, the optimal quantity depends only on the ratio of the cost of being short to the total cost of being wrong in either direction.
topics.title: The Newsvendor Quantity and the Critical Ratio

subjects.description: PLC sequencing, interlocks, sensors, drives, and safe automated production.
subjects.name: Industrial Automation & PLC Systems

topics.summary: PLC Sequence Logic and Safe Interlocks: A PLC sequence advances machine states only when the required permissives are true and faults or unsafe conditions force a defined safe state.
topics.title: PLC Sequence Logic and Safe Interlocks

topics.summary: Alarm Management: Rates, Priorities and Deadbands: An alarm is a demand for operator action, and the discipline is arithmetic as much as ergonomics: sustainable rates, distinct priorities, and deadbands that stop chattering signals from consuming both.
topics.title: Alarm Management: Rates, Priorities and Deadbands

topics.summary: Industrial Networks: Determinism and Scan Cycles: Control networks are judged not by average speed but by worst-case delivery - a 10 ms guaranteed cycle beats a 1 ms average with jitter, because control loops live on the guarantee.
topics.title: Industrial Networks: Determinism and Scan Cycles

topics.summary: Scan Time and Worst-Case Input-to-Output Latency: A PLC's response to an input is not instant: the worst case is two scan cycles plus input filter and output delays, and safety functions are verified against that number.
topics.title: Scan Time and Worst-Case Input-to-Output Latency

subjects.description: Lift, drag, stability, performance, and the forces governing aircraft flight.
subjects.name: Aerodynamics & Flight Mechanics

topics.summary: Lift, Dynamic Pressure, and Wing Area: For a specified flight condition, lift scales with dynamic pressure, reference area, and lift coefficient.
topics.title: Lift, Dynamic Pressure, and Wing Area

topics.summary: The Drag Polar and Best Glide Speed: An aircraft's drag is a baseline plus the price of lift, and the polar's minimum-drag point hands pilots the best glide speed and engineers the maximum lift-to-drag ratio.
topics.title: The Drag Polar and Best Glide Speed

topics.summary: Stall Speed and Load Factor in Turns: Stall is an angle-of-attack event, but the airspeed at which it arrives grows with the square root of load factor - which is why steep turns and turbulence pull stalls out of comfortable flight.
topics.title: Stall Speed and Load Factor in Turns

topics.summary: Induced Drag, Aspect Ratio and the Lift-to-Drag Trade: Wings make lift by deflecting air downward, and that same mechanism produces drag that falls as the wing gets longer and thinner - which is why gliders have long wings and fighters do not.
topics.title: Induced Drag, Aspect Ratio and the Lift-to-Drag Trade

subjects.description: Phase transformations, microstructure, heat treatment, and metal properties.
subjects.name: Physical Metallurgy & Heat Treatment

topics.summary: Lever Rule for Two-Phase Microstructures: Within a two-phase region of an equilibrium phase diagram, tie-line distances determine phase fractions by mass balance.
topics.title: Lever Rule for Two-Phase Microstructures

topics.summary: TTT Diagrams and Hardenability: Austenite's fate is a race against the TTT diagram's noses: quench fast enough to dodge pearlite and bainite, and the trapped carbon freezes into martensite - if the section is thick enough to stay fast at its core.
topics.title: TTT Diagrams and Hardenability

topics.summary: Annealing, Normalizing and Quenching: Microstructure Control: Heat treatment is scheduled microstructure: the same steel becomes soft and workable, strong and tough, or hard and brittle depending on how hot, how long, and - above all - how fast it cools.
topics.title: Annealing, Normalizing and Quenching: Microstructure Control

topics.summary: Quench Severity and Section Size: Getting Past the Pearlite Nose: A steel hardens only if its cooling curve reaches the martensite range before the pearlite transformation can start, and section size, quench medium and thermal diffusivity decide whether it does.
topics.title: Quench Severity and Section Size: Getting Past the Pearlite Nose

subjects.description: Polymer structure, molecular weight, rheology, extrusion, moulding, and composites.
subjects.name: Polymer Science & Processing

topics.summary: Power-Law Rheology in Polymer Processing: Many polymer melts are shear-thinning; a power-law model relates shear stress to shear rate over a limited processing range.
topics.title: Power-Law Rheology in Polymer Processing

topics.summary: Injection Moulding: Clamp Force and Projected Area: The clamp exists for one job - hold the mould shut against melt pressure pushing on the projected area - and sizing it is a pressure-times-area calculation with a safety factor.
topics.title: Injection Moulding: Clamp Force and Projected Area

topics.summary: Extrusion: Screw Output and Drag Flow: A single-screw extruder is a viscous drag pump: the rotating screw drags melt forward at a rate set by geometry and speed, minus a pressure-driven backflow.
topics.title: Extrusion: Screw Output and Drag Flow

topics.summary: Cooling Time and Its Share of the Moulding Cycle: Injection moulding cycle time is dominated by cooling, and cooling time grows with the square of wall thickness - which is why thin walls are cheap and thick ones are not.
topics.title: Cooling Time and Its Share of the Moulding Cycle

subjects.description: Porous-media flow, reserves, pressure support, well performance, and recovery.
subjects.name: Reservoir Engineering

topics.summary: Darcy Flow Through a Porous Reservoir: Darcy's law relates single-phase flow through a porous medium to permeability, area, pressure gradient, and viscosity.
topics.title: Darcy Flow Through a Porous Reservoir

topics.summary: Volumetric Reserves: STOIIP and Recovery Factor: Original oil in place is rock geometry times pore space times hydrocarbon saturation, corrected to surface conditions - and recoverable reserves are only the fraction physics and economics allow out.
topics.title: Volumetric Reserves: STOIIP and Recovery Factor

topics.summary: Material Balance and Drive Mechanisms: The reservoir is a closed accounting system: what leaves the pore space must equal what expands into it - and which term balances the books identifies the drive mechanism.
topics.title: Material Balance and Drive Mechanisms

topics.summary: Radial Flow into a Well and the Log-Term Insensitivity: Steady radial flow into a well depends only logarithmically on the drainage radius, which is why infill wells add far less production than a linear estimate suggests.
topics.title: Radial Flow into a Well and the Log-Term Insensitivity

subjects.description: Ore-body evaluation, mine design, equipment, ventilation, and responsible closure.
subjects.name: Mine Planning & Operations

topics.summary: Stripping Ratio and Open-Pit Mine Planning: Stripping ratio compares waste removed with ore recovered and is one input to an economic open-pit limit.
topics.title: Stripping Ratio and Open-Pit Mine Planning

topics.summary: Blasting Design: Powder Factor, Burden and Fragmentation: A production blast is engineered rock-breaking: burden and spacing set the broken volume per hole, and the powder factor prices the energy that fragments it.
topics.title: Blasting Design: Powder Factor, Burden and Fragmentation

topics.summary: Haulage Cycles: Truck Productivity and Fleet Matching: A haul fleet's output is trucks times trips times payload, and matching the loader's capacity to the trucks' cycle time is what turns equipment rates into tonnes per shift.
topics.title: Haulage Cycles: Truck Productivity and Fleet Matching

topics.summary: Cut-Off Grade and Break-Even Economics: The grade at which a tonne of ore pays for its own mining and processing is a single equation, and it moves with the metal price - which is why reserves are re-reported whenever prices change.
topics.title: Cut-Off Grade and Break-Even Economics

subjects.description: Cell growth, bioreactors, mass transfer, scale-up, and process monitoring.
subjects.name: Bioprocess Engineering

topics.summary: Monod Growth Kinetics in a Bioreactor: The Monod model describes specific microbial growth rate as substrate concentration rises toward a maximum.
topics.title: Monod Growth Kinetics in a Bioreactor

topics.summary: Oxygen Transfer: kLa and the Fermenter Oxygen Balance: Aerobic fermentation is usually oxygen-limited, and the transfer rate from bubble to broth - kLa times the driving force - must meet the culture's uptake or the cells downshift.
topics.title: Oxygen Transfer: kLa and the Fermenter Oxygen Balance

topics.summary: Bioreactor Scale-Up: Constant Power per Volume: Geometric scale-up multiplies volume by the cube of the size ratio, so no operating variable survives unchanged - the scale-up criterion chooses which physics to hold constant, and mixing power per volume is the usual vote.
topics.title: Bioreactor Scale-Up: Constant Power per Volume

topics.summary: Sterilisation: D-Value, Del Factor and the Temperature Trade: Thermal sterilisation is a log-reduction calculation: the hold time follows from the initial bioburden, the target sterility and the D-value at the chosen temperature.
topics.title: Sterilisation: D-Value, Del Factor and the Temperature Trade

subjects.description: Physiological signals, sensors, medical-device safety, calibration, and clinical context.
subjects.name: Biomedical Instrumentation & Devices

topics.summary: Instrumentation Amplifier for a Differential Biopotential: An instrumentation amplifier raises a small differential sensor signal while rejecting common-mode voltage, subject to range and safety constraints.
topics.title: Instrumentation Amplifier for a Differential Biopotential

topics.summary: ECG Signal Chain: Bandwidth and Common-Mode Rejection: An ECG front end must pass a 1 mV, 0.05-150 Hz differential signal sitting on volts of 50 Hz interference picked up by the body - a job for bandwidth discipline and common-mode rejection.
topics.title: ECG Signal Chain: Bandwidth and Common-Mode Rejection

topics.summary: Defibrillator Energy Delivery and Transthoracic Impedance: A defibrillator dumps a controlled joule-count through the chest, and the current that actually reaches the heart depends on energy, waveform and the patient's transthoracic impedance.
topics.title: Defibrillator Energy Delivery and Transthoracic Impedance

topics.summary: Leakage Currents and the Safety Limit That Decides Circuit Values: Patient safety in medical electronics is quantified in microamps: the current that can flow through a patient at mains frequency is set by capacitance and voltage, and it constrains isolation design directly.
topics.title: Leakage Currents and the Safety Limit That Decides Circuit Values

subjects.description: Heat and mass transfer, preservation, hygienic design, and food-safety controls.
subjects.name: Food Process Engineering & Safety

topics.summary: Decimal Reduction Time in Thermal Preservation: The decimal reduction time D is the exposure time at a specified temperature needed for a one-log reduction of a target organism.
topics.title: Decimal Reduction Time in Thermal Preservation

topics.summary: Water Activity and Microbial Growth Limits: Microbes grow on available water, not total water: water activity - the vapour-pressure ratio - is the number that decides who can grow, and drying, salting and sugaring all attack it.
topics.title: Water Activity and Microbial Growth Limits

topics.summary: Cold-Store Refrigeration Load: Product Cooling Duty: A cold room's compressor is sized by adding up every heat stream - product cooling first among them - and the product term is a simple sensible-heat rate that scheduling can flatten.
topics.title: Cold-Store Refrigeration Load: Product Cooling Duty

topics.summary: Freezing Time and the Plank Equation: Freezing is heat conduction out of a growing ice front, and the time it takes scales with thickness squared - which is why blast freezing thin products is dramatically faster.
topics.title: Freezing Time and the Plank Equation

subjects.description: Farm power, implement selection, irrigation efficiency, and post-harvest systems.
subjects.name: Agricultural Machinery & Irrigation Systems

topics.summary: Field Capacity and Field Efficiency: Field efficiency compares measured effective field capacity with theoretical capacity based on implement width and travel speed.
topics.title: Field Capacity and Field Efficiency

topics.summary: Sprayer Calibration: Application Rate from Nozzle, Speed and Spacing: A sprayer delivers what its calibration says, not what its label says: application rate follows from nozzle output divided by the ground area each nozzle covers per minute.
topics.title: Sprayer Calibration: Application Rate from Nozzle, Speed and Spacing

topics.summary: Irrigation Scheduling: Soil Moisture Depletion and Refill Amount: The soil is a reservoir between field capacity and wilting point, and scheduling means irrigating when depletion reaches the managed allowable - then refilling exactly the deficit.
topics.title: Irrigation Scheduling: Soil Moisture Depletion and Refill Amount

topics.summary: Tillage Draft, Implement Width and Tractor Power: The force needed to pull a tillage implement through soil depends on the soil's resistance, the working width and the depth, and multiplying by speed converts it into the power the tractor must deliver.
topics.title: Tillage Draft, Implement Width and Tractor Power

subjects.description: Ship resistance, propellers, engines, auxiliary systems, and operational safety.
subjects.name: Marine Propulsion & Power Systems

topics.summary: Shaft Power from Torque and Rotational Speed: A rotating shaft transmits power equal to torque multiplied by angular speed; propulsive power delivered to the water is affected by losses.
topics.title: Shaft Power from Torque and Rotational Speed

topics.summary: Propeller Slip, Pitch and Theoretical Speed: A propeller is a screw in a fluid that gives way: its theoretical speed comes from pitch times RPM, and the shortfall against actual speed - slip - measures the thrust being made.
topics.title: Propeller Slip, Pitch and Theoretical Speed

topics.summary: Ship Resistance Components and Effective Power: A hull's total resistance is the sum of friction, waves and appendages, and the effective power to overcome it at speed - divided by the propulsive coefficient - becomes the shaft power the engine room must supply.
topics.title: Ship Resistance Components and Effective Power

topics.summary: The Propeller Law and the Cost of Speed: A ship's power demand rises with the cube of propeller speed, so a modest reduction in service speed saves a disproportionate amount of fuel - the single largest lever in shipping economics.
topics.title: The Propeller Law and the Cost of Speed

subjects.description: Fibre properties, yarn formation, fabric construction, dyeing, and process quality.
subjects.name: Textile Fibre & Fabric Engineering

topics.summary: Yarn Linear Density and Tex: Tex expresses yarn mass in grams per kilometre, allowing a direct comparison of linear density across yarns.
topics.title: Yarn Linear Density and Tex

topics.summary: Fabric Cover: Yarn Spacing, Diameter and Permeability: How much of a fabric's area is yarn rather than hole governs its look, hand, air and water behaviour - and cover is computed from yarn diameter against spacing, system by system.
topics.title: Fabric Cover: Yarn Spacing, Diameter and Permeability

topics.summary: Twist: Helix Angle and Yarn Strength: Twist binds staple fibres into a coherent yarn, and its geometry - the surface helix angle - explains why strength rises with twist to an optimum and then falls away.
topics.title: Twist: Helix Angle and Yarn Strength

topics.summary: Loom Production Rate and Weaving Efficiency: How much fabric a loom produces follows from its speed and the picks per unit length, with an efficiency factor for stops - a calculation that decides machine numbers and delivery dates.
topics.title: Loom Production Rate and Weaving Efficiency

subjects.description: Solar and wind conversion, storage, grid integration, and lifecycle performance.
subjects.name: Renewable Energy Systems & Storage

topics.summary: Capacity Factor for Renewable Generation: Capacity factor compares energy actually generated over a period with the energy that would be produced at rated power continuously.
topics.title: Capacity Factor for Renewable Generation

topics.summary: The Betz Limit and Wind-Turbine Power: Wind power scales with the cube of speed and the swept area, but physics caps the extractable share at 59.3% - the Betz limit - before any machine inefficiency is counted.
topics.title: The Betz Limit and Wind-Turbine Power

topics.summary: PV Array Sizing: Peak Sun Hours and System Derates: A PV array's daily energy is its rating times the site's peak sun hours times a stack of loss factors - an arithmetic that sizes arrays, batteries and economics from one irradiation number.
topics.title: PV Array Sizing: Peak Sun Hours and System Derates

topics.summary: Storage Sizing and Round-Trip Efficiency on a Renewable System: Matching variable generation to demand is an energy balance, and round-trip efficiency means each stored kilowatt hour costs more than one to put in.
topics.title: Storage Sizing and Round-Trip Efficiency on a Renewable System
